content.text:
Re-traced every finding against the actual PR-head code and dependencies. The verification held most of them, **withdrew none outright, and upgraded one substantially** — the redundant-provider item turned out to hide a real regional regression I'd only hand-waved before. Evidence per finding below.

## The headline: #2 is worse than "redundant" — it narrows origins (verified)

I traced all three facts:
- **App-level provider is unconditional and app-wide.** `_app-config/index.tsx:131`→`154`: inside the main `return (`, no `isPreview` guard, `<ContentfulLivePreviewProvider locale={locale} enableInspectorMode enableLiveUpdates>` wraps `{children}`. Locale is `locals.locale?.id ?? 'en-US'` (line 111). So inspector + live-updates are **already on for every route**, and it passes **no `targetOrigin`**.
- **The SDK default `targetOrigin` is *two* origins.** The shipped chunks contain both `https://app.contentful.com` **and** `https://app.eu.contentful.com` (grep of `node_modules/@contentful/live-preview/dist`). Omitting the prop (as `_app-config` does) accepts both.
- **Both PR pages hardcode a *single* origin.** `contentfulPreview.tsx:166` and `experience.tsx:78`: `targetOrigin="https://app.contentful.com"`.

**Verified conclusion:** the per-page providers are (a) redundant — inspector/live-updates are already enabled app-wide with the same locale — and worse, (b) they **override `targetOrigin` down to a single origin, dropping `app.eu.contentful.com`** for their subtree. If Zimmermann's Contentful space is on the **EU instance**, editors previewing from `app.eu.contentful.com` would have their `postMessage`s rejected — **live preview silently breaks on the exact route built to enable it, EU-only.** That trips the multi-region rule in AGENTS.md. This is now the one genuinely valuable, act-before-merge finding — and the fix is mostly *deletion* (drop the per-page providers; if an origin restriction is actually wanted, set it once on the app-level provider and include the EU origin). **Status: UPGRADED, high value.**

## Verification ledger — the rest

|---|---------|------------------------|--------|

=== .docs/integration/01-sfcc.md — environment/target section ===
15:- Google reCAPTCHA — browser-side script load on register/login forms; MRT-side token verification before SCAPI submission
17:At migration, only the customer's email and Omneo ID are stored in SFCC. Name, phone, addresses, and communication preferences come from Omneo at login (DMU-004). Order history comes from MuleSoft via the MRT proxy, not from SFCC (DMU-007).
23:- Booxi appointment booking — MRT-mediated (PWA → MRT → Booxi), not a SFCC flow
44:- **Managed Runtime.** The PWA Kit Node layer hosts the SSR pipeline and routes SLAS private-client calls through the server-side proxy.
50:- **Private client credentials.** The SLAS client secret is an MRT environment variable and never reaches the browser. The authorisation code exchange goes through the MRT private-client proxy (`privateClientProxyEndpoint`). The SLAS client ID and SCAPI short code stay in the bundle as public identifiers.
63:- **Tokens are channel-scoped.** A token issued for `zimm-au` is not valid for `zimm-uk` — this is a hard SLAS platform constraint. On a storefront switch the SSR layer performs a fresh authorisation for the destination channel using the SLAS Trusted System on Behalf (TSOB) flow: it calls `getTrustedSystemAccessToken` with the shopper's `login_id`, which issues a new channel-scoped token server-side without prompting the customer. A registered shopper stays signed in transparently. A guest session does not carry over — guest tokens and baskets are site-scoped. **TSOB rate limit:** SLAS returns HTTP 409 if multiple TSOB calls are made for the same shopper within a 3-second window — the SSR layer must not fire duplicate TSOB calls on rapid storefront switches (debounce or dedupe at the MRT layer).
85:- On submit, the reCAPTCHA token is sent alongside the form data to the MRT layer. The MRT layer verifies the token against Google's `siteverify` endpoint (using the secret key held as the `RECAPTCHA_SECRET_KEY` MRT environment variable) before forwarding the request to SCAPI. The secret key never reaches the browser.
86:- The site key is set per environment as `RECAPTCHA_SITE_KEY` (MRT environment variable, public). The secret key is held as `RECAPTCHA_SECRET_KEY` (MRT environment variable, server-only).
115:- Per-environment SLAS client ID and SCAPI short code remain outstanding — see §11 item 2.
133:- SLAS private-client flow — the authorisation code exchange is proxied through MRT so the client secret never reaches the browser.

1	# yaml-language-server: $schema=https://coderabbit.ai/integrations/schema.v2.json
2	# .coderabbit.yaml — Zimmermann PWA Kit
3	# CodeRabbit configuration for AI-assisted PR review
4	# Docs: https://docs.coderabbit.ai/configuration
5	#
6	# Paths target this slim overrides project: `overrides/app/...` (not the upstream monorepo
7	# `packages/template-retail-react-app/app/...`). Hooks under `overrides/` are `.ts` per the
8	# TypeScript-only rule.
9	#
10	# NOTE: `version: "2"` and a top-level `custom_instructions:` block previously lived here.
11	# Neither key exists in the current schema (schema.v2.json) — confirmed by validating
12	# against the published schema and cross-checking real production configs (appsmith,
13	# bruno, MONAI), none of which use either key. custom_instructions's 12 rules have been
14	# migrated to the path_instructions entry below so they actually take effect.
15	
16	# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
17	# LANGUAGE & TONE
18	# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
19	language: "en-US"
20	
21	reviews:
22	  # Post a high-level summary on every PR
23	  high_level_summary: true
24	
25	  # Post a poem... no. We're engineers.
26	  poem: false
27	
28	  # Collapse walkthrough for smaller PRs to reduce noise
29	  collapse_walkthrough: false
30	
31	  # Request changes (not just comment) when critical issues found
32	  request_changes_workflow: true
33	
34	  # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
35	  # PROFILE — sets the overall review strictness
36	  # "assertive" = CodeRabbit will push back harder on issues
37	  # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
38	  profile: "assertive"
39	
40	  # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
41	  # PATH FILTERS — excludes mechanically-generated/derived files from
42	  # review scope entirely (distinct from path_instructions above, which
43	  # only changes review *criteria*, not whether a file is reviewed at
44	  # all). These files are regenerated from other source files already
45	  # covered by path_instructions/code_guidelines below — reviewing the
46	  # derived copy too is redundant, and scripts/hooks/pre-commit already
47	  # blocks hand-editing them directly, so review findings on them can't
48	  # be actioned there anyway. Excluding lock files per CodeRabbit's own
49	  # recommendation (docs.coderabbit.ai/guides/review-instructions).
50	  # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
51	  path_filters:
52	    - "!package-lock.json"
53	    # Generated by scripts/syncCursorRules.mjs from .claude/rules/*.md + AGENTS.md
54	    - "!.cursor/rules/**"
55	    - "!.vscode/instructions/**"
56	    - "!.github/copilot-instructions.md"
57	    # Generated by scripts/generateRegistry.mjs from overrides/app/
58	    - "!.claude/registry/*.md"
59	
60	  # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
61	  # PATH-LEVEL INSTRUCTIONS
62	  # This is the most powerful CodeRabbit feature for this project.
63	  # Different review instructions per file path.
64	  # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
65	  path_instructions:
66	    # ── Repo-wide baseline (was a non-functional top-level `custom_instructions:`
67	    #    key — migrated here since path_instructions is the mechanism that
68	    #    actually exists in the schema; matching entries apply cumulatively
69	    #    alongside the more specific ones below) ─────────────
70	    - path: "overrides/**"
71	      instructions: |
72	        This is a Salesforce Commerce Cloud PWA Kit storefront for Zimmermann luxury fashion.
73	        This is a slim overrides project on `@salesforce/retail-react-app` v10 (not a fork).
74	        The stack is React 18, Chakra UI v2, React Query v4, React Hook Form v7, and Express SSR
75	        on Salesforce Managed Runtime.
76	
77	        For every PR, check:
78	
79	        1. TYPESCRIPT-ONLY INSIDE overrides/ — Every file created or modified under `overrides/`
80	           must use `.ts` or `.tsx`. Flag any `.js`/`.jsx` introduced inside `overrides/`.
81	
82	        2. SSR SAFETY — Any hook or component that accesses window, document, localStorage, or
83	           sessionStorage must have a typeof window !== 'undefined' guard. SSR failures cause
84	           complete page breakdowns.
85	
86	        3. REACT QUERY CACHE — Any mutation that changes basket, customer, or order state must
87	           call queryClient.invalidateQueries() with the correct query key. Missing invalidations
88	           cause stale data that persists until page reload.
89	
90	        4. CHAKRA THEME USAGE — No inline style values for colours, spacing, or typography.
91	           All values must reference theme tokens (e.g. "brand.primary" not "#1A1A1A").
92	           Hard-coded values bypass the design system and break brand consistency.
93	
94	        5. LOCALE AWARENESS — No hardcoded strings in JSX. All user-facing copy must use
95	           react-intl's useIntl() hook and a message ID. Zimmermann serves 18 locales across
96	           6 regions.
97	
98	        6. MULTI-REGION SAFETY — No hardcoded currency symbols, country codes, or locale strings.
99	           Zimmermann serves AU, US, UK, EU, ME, HK (7–8 SFCC sites — US split is TBC).
100	           Use useMultiSite() for site context.
101	
102	        7. EINSTEIN & DATACLOUD EVENTS — Any user interaction that qualifies as a commerce event
103	           (view product, add to cart, begin checkout, click recommendation) must fire the
104	           corresponding Einstein and DataCloud event. Missing events corrupt analytics and
105	           personalisation data.
106	
107	        8. ACCESSIBILITY — Target WCAG 2.2 AA. All interactive elements must have accessible
108	           labels. Images must have alt text. Focus management must be correct in modals and
109	           drawers.
110	
111	        9. PERFORMANCE — Mobile page speed is a top priority. Flag any new synchronous blocking
112	           operations in the SSR render path. Flag any new third-party scripts loaded without
113	           async/defer. Flag images rendered at full resolution where a thumbnail size is used.
114	
115	        10. NO CONSOLE LOGS IN PRODUCTION CODE — Debug logs must be removed before merge.
116	            Sensitive data (tokens, customer PII, basket contents) must never be logged.
117	
118	        11. CLAUDE CODE PROVENANCE — If a PR description or commit message indicates Claude Code CLI
119	            was used to generate the changes, apply heightened scrutiny to shared hooks and
120	            components. Verify the scope of changes matches what was described in the PR.
121	
122	        12. CONVENTIONAL COMMITS — Every commit message in this PR must follow the format:
123	            type(scope): description
124	            Valid types: feat, fix, docs, style, refactor, perf, test, build, ci, chore, upstream-sync
125	            Scope is optional but encouraged (e.g. product-tile, checkout, global-e, contentful).
126	            If any commit does not follow this format (excluding Merge and Revert commits), flag it
127	            and request it be amended before merge. A non-compliant commit message will produce an
128	            incorrect or unclassifiable changelog entry.
129

133	        TIER 1 — DESIGN SYSTEM FROZEN FILE.

138	        - Any font size, weight, or family changes — flag what changed

140	        - Any breakpoint value changes — these affect every responsive component
141	        - Whether the change is additive (new token) or destructive (modifying existing token)
142

152	
153	        Every change requires:
154	        - Explicit audit of all import consumers: grep -r "use-current-basket" overrides/
155	        - Confirmation that the return shape has not changed

157	        - A note in the PR description listing every consumer that was tested

163	
164	        Check for:

166	        - Changes to token handling or SLAS auth flow

170	      instructions: |

173	
174	        Check for:

176	        - Changes to the navigate() function signature
177	        - Any new required parameters

179	    - path: "overrides/app/hooks/use-multi-site.ts"
180	      instructions: |
181	        TIER 1 — useMultiSite drives regional site, locale, and currency resolution.
182	        This affects all Zimmermann regional sites (AU, US, UK, EU, ME, HK — 7–8 storefronts).
183	
184	        Check for:
185	        - Any hardcoded locale or currency values
186	        - Changes to site alias resolution logic
187	        - Whether changes have been tested against all configured locales, not just en-AU

190	    - path: "config/**"
191	      instructions: |
192	        TIER 1 — RUNTIME CONFIGURATION. These files control feature flags, API endpoints,
193	        and proxy routing for all environments.
194	
195	        Check for:
196	        - Any hardcoded API keys, secrets, or credentials — immediate block, must be in env vars
197	        - Any feature flag default that differs from the agreed rollout state

199	        - Whether a change in default.js was intentionally not overridden in production.js

202	      instructions: |

209	        - Any change to ssrOnly or ssrShared path arrays

212	      instructions: |

214	
215	        Check for:

217	        - Any new secret references — confirm the secret exists in GitHub Secrets for all environments
218	        - Any change to the deploy or activate steps — flag what changes and why
219	        - Whether the change maintains the feature → develop → main promotion flow
220	
221	    # ── Tier 1: SSR server ──────────────────────────────────
222	    - path: "overrides/app/ssr.js"
223	      instructions: |
224	        TIER 1 — SSR SERVER ENTRY. This file configures the Express server that runs on
225	        Salesforce Managed Runtime. A broken ssr.js takes down the entire storefront.
226	
227	        Check for:
228	        - Any change to createApp() options — these affect all routes
229	        - Any new middleware that could affect response headers or caching
230	        - Any environment-specific logic that is missing an environment check
231	        - Whether the change has been tested with SSR enabled (not just client-side)
232	
233	    # ── Tier 2: Global shell ─────────────────────────────────
234	    - path: "overrides/app/components/header/**"
235	      instructions: |
236	        TIER 2 — GLOBAL HEADER. This renders on every page. Review as if this is production-critical.
237	
238	        Check for:
239	        - Any change to the navigation data structure consumed from useNavigation
240	        - Any new prop added to a child component — confirm it's optional with a sensible default
241	        - Mobile/desktop breakpoint logic — confirm both viewports are covered
242	        - Accessibility: keyboard navigation, focus management, aria labels on interactive elements
243	        - Any new external script or asset load — this adds to page weight on every route
244	
245	    - path: "overrides/app/routes.tsx"
246	      instructions: |
247	        TIER 2 — ROUTE CONFIGURATION. Adding, removing, or reordering routes affects
248	        SEO, analytics, and every developer's feature work.
249	
250	        Check for:
251	        - Any route removal — confirm a redirect exists before the route is dropped
252	        - Any path change — confirm SEO redirect mapping has been updated
253	        - Whether new routes use code splitting (@loadable/component)
254	        - Whether SSR is intentionally disabled on any new route (rare — flag if so)
255	        - Whether locale-prefixed path generation is still intact
256	
257	    # ── Tier 2: Shared product components ───────────────────
258	    - path: "overrides/app/components/product-tile/**"
259	      instructions: |
260	        TIER 2 — SHARED PRODUCT TILE. Used on PLP, search results, wishlists,
261	        recommendation carousels, and the homepage. Changes affect multiple pages.
262	
263	        Check for:
264	        - Any change to required props — will break all consumers if made non-optional
265	        - Any new data dependency from a hook — confirm that hook is available in all
266	          contexts where product-tile is rendered (PLP, search, wishlist, recommendations)
267	        - Image lazy loading — confirm it's still applied
268	        - Wishlist toggle functionality — confirm it still works for both guest and registered users
269	
270	    - path: "overrides/app/components/display-price/**"
271	      instructions: |
272	        TIER 2 — PRICE DISPLAY. Used across PDP, PLP, cart, and order history.
273	        Price display bugs are immediately visible to customers.
274	
275	        Check for:
276	        - Correct handling of all price types: regular, sale/strikethrough, promotional, range
277	        - Currency formatting — confirm it uses the locale-aware formatter, not hardcoded symbols
278	        - Sale price display — confirm strikethrough logic is not broken
279	
280	    # ── Checkout pages ───────────────────────────────────────
281	    - path: "overrides/app/pages/checkout/**"
282	      instructions: |
283	        SQUAD A — CHECKOUT. This is the highest-revenue-risk area of the codebase.
284	
285	        Check for:
286	        - Any change to the basket mutation sequence — order of operations matters for SCAPI
287	        - Payment handling — confirm no payment data is logged or exposed in error messages
288	        - 3DS / async payment flow — confirm the PaymentProcessing intermediate page still works
289	        - BOPIS vs. standard delivery toggle — confirm switching modes doesn't corrupt shipment data
290	        - Guest vs. registered checkout state — confirm both flows still work after the change
291	        - Form validation — confirm required fields still prevent submission when empty
292	
293	    # ── PDP / PLP ────────────────────────────────────────────
294	    - path: "overrides/app/pages/product-detail/**"
295	      instructions: |
296	        SQUAD B — PDP. The product detail page is the primary conversion entry point.
297	
298	        Check for:
299	        - Variant selection logic — confirm all variation attributes still resolve correctly
300	        - Add to cart — confirm ATC still fires the Einstein sendAddToCart event
301	        - Image gallery — confirm mobile swipe and zoom still work after any changes
302	        - SSR data prefetch — confirm useProduct is still being prefetched server-side
303	        - Structured data — confirm schema.org Product markup is still present in the output
304	
305	    - path: "overrides/app/pages/product-list/**"
306	      instructions: |
307	        SQUAD B — PLP. Faceted search, refinements, and sorting are SEO-critical.
308	
309	        Check for:
310	        - URL-based refinement state — confirm filters are reflected in the URL for SEO
311	        - Pagination — confirm URL-based pagination is intact (not scroll-based pagination)
312	        - Refinement removal — confirm the "clear all" and individual remove buttons still work
313	        - Page Designer slot — confirm the promotional banner slot still renders
314	
315	    # ── QA feature files ─────────────────────────────────────
316	    - path: "e2e/features/**"
317	      instructions: |
318	        GHERKIN FEATURE FILES — source of truth for QA. Lead QA must validate before
319	        the paired Playwright spec is generated.
320	
321	        Check for:
322	        - Jira traceability tag present: @SFCC-NNN
323	        - Area tag present: @checkout, @search, @account, @pdp, @plp, or @integrations
324	        - P0 journeys tagged @p0 — verify the scenario qualifies (checkout, ATC, auth, PDP variant)
325	        - No technical implementation detail in scenario steps — no selectors, URLs, or code references
326	        - At least one happy path and one failure/edge scenario per feature file
327	        - Background block used for shared preconditions, not repeated in each scenario
328	        - File under 150 lines — flag if exceeded, suggest splitting by scenario group
329	        - Baseline regression files (in regression/) are prefixed BASELINE- and use
330	          @baseline @regression tags (no Jira key tag)
331	        - DELTA comments present where SFCC behaviour is known to differ from Magento baseline
332	
333	    # ── General hooks ────────────────────────────────────────
334	    - path: "overrides/app/hooks/**"
335	      instructions: |
336	        HOOKS — Shared application logic. Check every hook change for:
337	
338	        - Whether the return value shape has changed — even adding a key can cause
339	          consumer components to render differently if they spread the return value
340	        - Whether the hook adds a new required parameter — this is always a breaking change
341	        - Whether cleanup functions (useEffect return) are still present where needed
342	        - Whether the hook is safe to call during SSR (no window/document access without guards)
343	        - Whether React Query cache invalidation is correct after mutations
344	
345	  # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
346	  # TOOLS — static analysis CodeRabbit runs automatically
347	  # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
348	  tools:
349	    eslint:
350	      enabled: true
351	    # Detect hardcoded secrets
352	    gitleaks:
353	      enabled: true
354	    # Project-specific pattern rules — a11y (JSX) and naming/structure checks.
355	    # Tested locally with the ast-grep CLI against fixtures + real files before landing.
356	    ast-grep:
357	      rule_dirs:
358	        - ".coderabbit/ast-grep-rules"
359	      util_dirs:
360	        - ".coderabbit/ast-grep-rules/utils"
361	      essential_rules: true
362	    # npm/package-lock.json dependency vulnerability scanning (OSV.dev database)
363	    osvScanner:
364	      enabled: true
365	    # React-specific security/performance/correctness/accessibility scanner
366	    reactDoctor:
367	      enabled: true
368	    # Requires semgrep.yml in repo root (see that file) — payment-credential-logging
369	    # and unsanitized dangerouslySetInnerHTML taint/pattern rules, tested locally.
370	    semgrep:
371	      enabled: true
372	      config_file: "semgrep.yml"
373	
374	  # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
375	  # AUTO-REVIEW triggers
376	  # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
377	  auto_review:
378	    enabled: true
379	    # Review every push to a PR, not just on open
380	    auto_incremental_review: true
381	    # Don't waste review on draft PRs
382	    drafts: false
383	    # Ignore PRs that are purely dependency updates
384	    ignore_title_keywords:
385	      - "chore(deps)"
386	      - "dependabot"
387	
388	  # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
389	  # PRE-MERGE CHECKS — actual merge-blocking gates (requires
390	  # request_changes_workflow: true above to enforce `error` mode).
391	  # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
392	  pre_merge_checks:
393	    # Blunt repo-wide docstring % gate is intentionally OFF — it can't be
394	    # path-scoped, so it can't distinguish shared components/exported hooks
395	    # (which need JSDoc per components.md) from leaf components (which don't).
396	    # Replaced by the docstring-convention-compliance custom_check below.
397	    docstrings:
398	      mode: "off"
399	    title:
400	      mode: error
401	      requirements: >-
402	        Must follow Conventional Commits format: type(scope): description.
403	        Valid types: feat, fix, docs, style, refactor, perf, test, build, ci,
404	        chore, upstream-sync. Scope is optional but encouraged.
405	    description:
406	      mode: error
407	    # Jira Forge app is not yet installed in the Atlassian instance — this has
408	    # nothing to assess against until that connection exists. Flip to `error`
409	    # once installed (see knowledge_base.jira below).
410	    issue_assessment:
411	      mode: warning
412	    custom_checks:
413	      - name: "Docstring convention compliance"
414	        mode: error
415	        instructions: >-
416	          Fail this check only if the PR adds or modifies (a) a component consumed
417	          by 2 or more callers (a shared component per protectedFiles.md/components.md),
418	          (b) an exported hook under overrides/app/hooks/**, or (c) a utility function
419	          with non-obvious behaviour — and the added/modified declaration does not
420	          have a JSDoc comment (hooks must include a @returns description).
421	          Do NOT fail for: leaf/single-consumer components, trivial or self-evident
422	          utilities, type-only files, test files, or story files. Pass if no
423	          qualifying declaration was added or modified in this PR.
424	
425	  # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
426	  # FINISHING TOUCHES — on-demand generation via PR checkbox or
427	  # @coderabbitai command
428	  # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
429	  finishing_touches:
430	    docstrings:
431	      enabled: true
432	
433	# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
434	# CHAT — allows developers to ask CodeRabbit questions in PR comments
435	# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
436	chat:
437	  auto_reply: true
438	
439	# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
440	# KNOWLEDGE BASE — external context sources
441	# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
442	knowledge_base:
443	  jira:
444	    # NOTE: this only scopes context once the Jira Forge app is installed and
445	    # connected via the Atlassian Marketplace — it does not establish that
446	    # connection itself. As of this config, the Forge app is NOT yet installed
447	    # in zimmermannworkboard.atlassian.net. Link a Jira issue by pasting its
448	    # URL into the PR description (no auto-detection from branch name).
449	    usage: enabled
450	    project_keys:
451	      - "SFCC"
452	  code_guidelines:
453	    # AGENTS.md is already covered by CodeRabbit's own default file patterns
454	    # (confirmed in docs) — listed explicitly anyway for visibility. The
455	    # .claude/rules/*.md files are NOT covered by any default pattern, and
456	    # AGENTS.md's markdown links to them are not resolved/followed by
457	    # CodeRabbit (it reads literal file content only), so without this they
458	    # would not be used as review criteria at all.
459	    enabled: true
460	    filePatterns:
461	      - "AGENTS.md"
462	      - files: ".claude/rules/conventions.md"
463	        applyTo: "overrides/**"
464	      - files: ".claude/rules/typescript.md"
465	        applyTo: "overrides/**"
466	      - files: ".claude/rules/css.md"
467	        applyTo: "overrides/**"
468	      - files: ".claude/rules/components.md"
469	        applyTo: "overrides/app/components/**,overrides/app/pages/**,overrides/app/hooks/**"
470	      - files: ".claude/rules/testing.md"
471	        applyTo: "overrides/**,e2e/**"
472	      - files: ".claude/rules/frozenFiles.md"
473	        applyTo: "**"
474	      - files: ".claude/rules/protectedFiles.md"
475	        applyTo: "**"
476	
477	# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
478	# CODE GENERATION — style guidance for finishing_touches.docstrings
479	# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
480	code_generation:
481	  docstrings:
482	    path_instructions:
483	      - path: "overrides/app/hooks/**"
484	        instructions: >-
485	          Every exported hook needs a JSDoc comment including a @returns
486	          description, per components.md > Hooks.
487	      - path: "overrides/app/components/**"
488	        instructions: >-
489	          Only generate JSDoc for components consumed by 2 or more callers
490	          (Tier 2 shared components per protectedFiles.md). Skip leaf,
491	          single-consumer components — components.md says the prop type is
492	          sufficient for those.
493

file.content:
# yaml-language-server: $schema=https://coderabbit.ai/integrations/schema.v2.json
# .coderabbit.yaml — Zimmermann PWA Kit
# CodeRabbit configuration for AI-assisted PR review
# Docs: https://docs.coderabbit.ai/configuration
#
# Paths target this slim overrides project: `overrides/app/...` (not the upstream monorepo
# `packages/template-retail-react-app/app/...`). Hooks under `overrides/` are `.ts` per the
# TypeScript-only rule.
#
# NOTE: `version: "2"` and a top-level `custom_instructions:` block previously lived here.
# Neither key exists in the current schema (schema.v2.json) — confirmed by validating
# against the published schema and cross-checking real production configs (appsmith,
# bruno, MONAI), none of which use either key. custom_instructions's 12 rules have been
# migrated to the path_instructions entry below so they actually take effect.

# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# LANGUAGE & TONE
# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
language: "en-US"

reviews:
  # Post a high-level summary on every PR
  high_level_summary: true

  # Post a poem... no. We're engineers.
  poem: false

  # Collapse walkthrough for smaller PRs to reduce noise
  collapse_walkthrough: false

  # Request changes (not just comment) when critical issues found
  request_changes_workflow: true

  # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  # PROFILE — sets the overall review strictness
  # "assertive" = CodeRabbit will push back harder on issues
  # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  profile: "assertive"

  # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  # PATH FILTERS — excludes mechanically-generated/derived files from
  # review scope entirely (distinct from path_instructions above, which
  # only changes review *criteria*, not whether a file is reviewed at
  # all). These files are regenerated from other source files already
  # covered by path_instructions/code_guidelines below — reviewing the
  # derived copy too is redundant, and scripts/hooks/pre-commit already
  # blocks hand-editing them directly, so review findings on them can't
  # be actioned there anyway. Excluding lock files per CodeRabbit's own
  # recommendation (docs.coderabbit.ai/guides/review-instructions).
  # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  path_filters:
    - "!package-lock.json"
    # Generated by scripts/syncCursorRules.mjs from .claude/rules/*.md + AGENTS.md
    - "!.cursor/rules/**"
    - "!.vscode/instructions/**"
    - "!.github/copilot-instructions.md"
    # Generated by scripts/generateRegistry.mjs from overrides/app/
    - "!.claude/registry/*.md"

  # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  # PATH-LEVEL INSTRUCTIONS
  # This is the most powerful CodeRabbit feature for this project.
  # Different review instructions per file path.
  # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  path_instructions:
    # ── Repo-wide baseline (was a non-functional top-level `custom_instructions:`
    #    key — migrated here since path_instructions is the mechanism that
    #    actually exists in the schema; matching entries apply cumulatively
    #    alongside the more specific ones below) ─────────────
    - path: "overrides/**"
      instructions: |
        This is a Salesforce Commerce Cloud PWA Kit storefront for Zimmermann luxury fashion.
        This is a slim overrides project on `@salesforce/retail-react-app` v10 (not a fork).
        The stack is React 18, Chakra UI v2, React Query v4, React Hook Form v7, and Express SSR
        on Salesforce Managed Runtime.

        For every PR, check:

        1. TYPESCRIPT-ONLY INSIDE overrides/ — Every file created or modified under `overrides/`
           must use `.ts` or `.tsx`. Flag any `.js`/`.jsx` introduced inside `overrides/`.

        2. SSR SAFETY — Any hook or component that accesses window, document, localStorage, or
           sessionStorage must have a typeof window !== 'undefined' guard. SSR failures cause
           complete page breakdowns.

        3. REACT QUERY CACHE — Any mutation that changes basket, customer, or order state must
           call queryClient.invalidateQueries() with the correct query key. Missing invalidations
           cause stale data that persists until page reload.

        4. CHAKRA THEME USAGE — No inline style values for colours, spacing, or typography.
           All values must reference theme tokens (e.g. "brand.primary" not "#1A1A1A").
           Hard-coded values bypass the design system and break brand consistency.

        5. LOCALE AWARENESS — No hardcoded strings in JSX. All user-facing copy must use
           react-intl's useIntl() hook and a message ID. Zimmermann serves 18 locales across
           6 regions.

        6. MULTI-REGION SAFETY — No hardcoded currency symbols, country codes, or locale strings.
           Zimmermann serves AU, US, UK, EU, ME, HK (7–8 SFCC sites — US split is TBC).
           Use useMultiSite() for site context.

        7. EINSTEIN & DATACLOUD EVENTS — Any user interaction that qualifies as a commerce event
           (view product, add to cart, begin checkout, click recommendation) must fire the
           corresponding Einstein and DataCloud event. Missing events corrupt analytics and
           personalisation data.

        8. ACCESSIBILITY — Target WCAG 2.2 AA. All interactive elements must have accessible
           labels. Images must have alt text. Focus management must be correct in modals and
           drawers.

        9. PERFORMANCE — Mobile page speed is a top priority. Flag any new synchronous blocking
           operations in the SSR render path. Flag any new third-party scripts loaded without
           async/defer. Flag images rendered at full resolution where a thumbnail size is used.

        10. NO CONSOLE LOGS IN PRODUCTION CODE — Debug logs must be removed before merge.
            Sensitive data (tokens, customer PII, basket contents) must never be logged.

        11. CLAUDE CODE PROVENANCE — If a PR description or commit message indicates Claude Code CLI
            was used to generate the changes, apply heightened scrutiny to shared hooks and
            components. Verify the scope of changes matches what was described in the PR.

        12. CONVENTIONAL COMMITS — Every commit message in this PR must follow the format:
            type(scope): description
            Valid types: feat, fix, docs, style, refactor, perf, test, build, ci, chore, upstream-sync
            Scope is optional but encouraged (e.g. product-tile, checkout, global-e, contentful).
            If any commit does not follow this format (excluding Merge and Revert commits), flag it
            and request it be amended before merge. A non-compliant commit message will produce an
            incorrect or unclassifiable changelog entry.

    # ── Tier 1: Design tokens ───────────────────────────────
    - path: "overrides/app/theme/foundation/**"
      instructions: |
        TIER 1 — DESIGN SYSTEM FROZEN FILE.
        This file contains Zimmermann brand design tokens. Treat every change with maximum scrutiny.

        Check for:
        - Any colour value changes — flag the old and new hex values explicitly
        - Any font size, weight, or family changes — flag what changed
        - Any spacing scale changes — note which scale values were modified
        - Any breakpoint value changes — these affect every responsive component
        - Whether the change is additive (new token) or destructive (modifying existing token)

        Destructive changes to existing tokens will affect every component in the design system.
        Always flag: "This change modifies an existing design token. Confirm with UI Designer that
        all consumers have been audited."

    # ── Tier 1: Shared critical hooks ───────────────────────
    - path: "overrides/app/hooks/use-current-basket.ts"
      instructions: |
        TIER 1 — HIGHEST RISK HOOK. useCurrentBasket is consumed by cart, checkout,
        order summary, promo code, and bonus product components simultaneously.

        Every change requires:
        - Explicit audit of all import consumers: grep -r "use-current-basket" overrides/
        - Confirmation that the return shape has not changed
        - Confirmation that guest basket and registered basket merge behaviour is unaffected
        - A note in the PR description listing every consumer that was tested

    - path: "overrides/app/hooks/use-current-customer.ts"
      instructions: |
        TIER 1 — useCurrentCustomer is the auth state source of truth.
        Any change affects login, registration, guest flow, and account pages simultaneously.

        Check for:
        - Changes to customerType or isGuest return values
        - Changes to token handling or SLAS auth flow
        - Any new side effects on mount or unmount

    - path: "overrides/app/hooks/use-navigation.ts"
      instructions: |
        TIER 1 — useNavigation is consumed by header, footer, drawer menu, and breadcrumbs.
        A broken navigation hook breaks the global shell on every page.

        Check for:
        - Changes to locale-aware URL construction
        - Changes to the navigate() function signature
        - Any new required parameters

    - path: "overrides/app/hooks/use-multi-site.ts"
      instructions: |
        TIER 1 — useMultiSite drives regional site, locale, and currency resolution.
        This affects all Zimmermann regional sites (AU, US, UK, EU, ME, HK — 7–8 storefronts).

        Check for:
        - Any hardcoded locale or currency values
        - Changes to site alias resolution logic
        - Whether changes have been tested against all configured locales, not just en-AU

    # ── Tier 1: Runtime config ───────────────────────────────
    - path: "config/**"
      instructions: |
        TIER 1 — RUNTIME CONFIGURATION. These files control feature flags, API endpoints,
        and proxy routing for all environments.

        Check for:
        - Any hardcoded API keys, secrets, or credentials — immediate block, must be in env vars
        - Any feature flag default that differs from the agreed rollout state
        - Any proxy host that differs between environment files — flag old vs. new value
        - Whether a change in default.js was intentionally not overridden in production.js

    - path: "mobify.config.js"
      instructions: |
        TIER 1 — MRT DEPLOYMENT CONFIG. Changes here affect what gets deployed to
        Salesforce Managed Runtime. A bad change can break all SSR or CDN routing.

        Check for:
        - Any change to projectSlug — a mismatch causes silent deploy failures
        - Any change to ssrParameters.proxyConfigs — verify host values match B2C instances
        - Any change to ssrOnly or ssrShared path arrays

    - path: ".github/workflows/**"
      instructions: |
        TIER 1 — CI/CD PIPELINE. Changes here affect every developer's ability to ship.

        Check for:
        - Any removal of existing test gates (lint, unit tests, Lighthouse CI, bundle size)
        - Any new secret references — confirm the secret exists in GitHub Secrets for all environments
        - Any change to the deploy or activate steps — flag what changes and why
        - Whether the change maintains the feature → develop → main promotion flow

    # ── Tier 1: SSR server ──────────────────────────────────
    - path: "overrides/app/ssr.js"
      instructions: |
        TIER 1 — SSR SERVER ENTRY. This file configures the Express server that runs on
        Salesforce Managed Runtime. A broken ssr.js takes down the entire storefront.

        Check for:
        - Any change to createApp() options — these affect all routes
        - Any new middleware that could affect response headers or caching
        - Any environment-specific logic that is missing an environment check
        - Whether the change has been tested with SSR enabled (not just client-side)

    # ── Tier 2: Global shell ─────────────────────────────────
    - path: "overrides/app/components/header/**"
      instructions: |
        TIER 2 — GLOBAL HEADER. This renders on every page. Review as if this is production-critical.

        Check for:
        - Any change to the navigation data structure consumed from useNavigation
        - Any new prop added to a child component — confirm it's optional with a sensible default
        - Mobile/desktop breakpoint logic — confirm both viewports are covered
        - Accessibility: keyboard navigation, focus management, aria labels on interactive elements
        - Any new external script or asset load — this adds to page weight on every route

    - path: "overrides/app/routes.tsx"
      instructions: |
        TIER 2 — ROUTE CONFIGURATION. Adding, removing, or reordering routes affects
        SEO, analytics, and every developer's feature work.

        Check for:
        - Any route removal — confirm a redirect exists before the route is dropped
        - Any path change — confirm SEO redirect mapping has been updated
        - Whether new routes use code splitting (@loadable/component)
        - Whether SSR is intentionally disabled on any new route (rare — flag if so)
        - Whether locale-prefixed path generation is still intact

    # ── Tier 2: Shared product components ───────────────────
    - path: "overrides/app/components/product-tile/**"
      instructions: |
        TIER 2 — SHARED PRODUCT TILE. Used on PLP, search results, wishlists,
        recommendation carousels, and the homepage. Changes affect multiple pages.

        Check for:
        - Any change to required props — will break all consumers if made non-optional
        - Any new data dependency from a hook — confirm that hook is available in all
          contexts where product-tile is rendered (PLP, search, wishlist, recommendations)
        - Image lazy loading — confirm it's still applied
        - Wishlist toggle functionality — confirm it still works for both guest and registered users

    - path: "overrides/app/components/display-price/**"
      instructions: |
        TIER 2 — PRICE DISPLAY. Used across PDP, PLP, cart, and order history.
        Price display bugs are immediately visible to customers.

        Check for:
        - Correct handling of all price types: regular, sale/strikethrough, promotional, range
        - Currency formatting — confirm it uses the locale-aware formatter, not hardcoded symbols
        - Sale price display — confirm strikethrough logic is not broken

    # ── Checkout pages ───────────────────────────────────────
    - path: "overrides/app/pages/checkout/**"
      instructions: |
        SQUAD A — CHECKOUT. This is the highest-revenue-risk area of the codebase.

        Check for:
        - Any change to the basket mutation sequence — order of operations matters for SCAPI
        - Payment handling — confirm no payment data is logged or exposed in error messages
        - 3DS / async payment flow — confirm the PaymentProcessing intermediate page still works
        - BOPIS vs. standard delivery toggle — confirm switching modes doesn't corrupt shipment data
        - Guest vs. registered checkout state — confirm both flows still work after the change
        - Form validation — confirm required fields still prevent submission when empty

    # ── PDP / PLP ────────────────────────────────────────────
    - path: "overrides/app/pages/product-detail/**"
      instructions: |
        SQUAD B — PDP. The product detail page is the primary conversion entry point.

        Check for:
        - Variant selection logic — confirm all variation attributes still resolve correctly
        - Add to cart — confirm ATC still fires the Einstein sendAddToCart event
        - Image gallery — confirm mobile swipe and zoom still work after any changes
        - SSR data prefetch — confirm useProduct is still being prefetched server-side
        - Structured data — confirm schema.org Product markup is still present in the output

    - path: "overrides/app/pages/product-list/**"
      instructions: |
        SQUAD B — PLP. Faceted search, refinements, and sorting are SEO-critical.

        Check for:
        - URL-based refinement state — confirm filters are reflected in the URL for SEO
        - Pagination — confirm URL-based pagination is intact (not scroll-based pagination)
        - Refinement removal — confirm the "clear all" and individual remove buttons still work
        - Page Designer slot — confirm the promotional banner slot still renders

    # ── QA feature files ─────────────────────────────────────
    - path: "e2e/features/**"
      instructions: |
        GHERKIN FEATURE FILES — source of truth for QA. Lead QA must validate before
        the paired Playwright spec is generated.

        Check for:
        - Jira traceability tag present: @SFCC-NNN
        - Area tag present: @checkout, @search, @account, @pdp, @plp, or @integrations
        - P0 journeys tagged @p0 — verify the scenario qualifies (checkout, ATC, auth, PDP variant)
        - No technical implementation detail in scenario steps — no selectors, URLs, or code references
        - At least one happy path and one failure/edge scenario per feature file
        - Background block used for shared preconditions, not repeated in each scenario
        - File under 150 lines — flag if exceeded, suggest splitting by scenario group
        - Baseline regression files (in regression/) are prefixed BASELINE- and use
          @baseline @regression tags (no Jira key tag)
        - DELTA comments present where SFCC behaviour is known to differ from Magento baseline

    # ── General hooks ────────────────────────────────────────
    - path: "overrides/app/hooks/**"
      instructions: |
        HOOKS — Shared application logic. Check every hook change for:

        - Whether the return value shape has changed — even adding a key can cause
          consumer components to render differently if they spread the return value
        - Whether the hook adds a new required parameter — this is always a breaking change
        - Whether cleanup functions (useEffect return) are still present where needed
        - Whether the hook is safe to call during SSR (no window/document access without guards)
        - Whether React Query cache invalidation is correct after mutations

  # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  # TOOLS — static analysis CodeRabbit runs automatically
  # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  tools:
    eslint:
      enabled: true
    # Detect hardcoded secrets
    gitleaks:
      enabled: true
    # Project-specific pattern rules — a11y (JSX) and naming/structure checks.
    # Tested locally with the ast-grep CLI against fixtures + real files before landing.
    ast-grep:
      rule_dirs:
        - ".coderabbit/ast-grep-rules"
      util_dirs:
        - ".coderabbit/ast-grep-rules/utils"
      essential_rules: true
    # npm/package-lock.json dependency vulnerability scanning (OSV.dev database)
    osvScanner:
      enabled: true
    # React-specific security/performance/correctness/accessibility scanner
    reactDoctor:
      enabled: true
    # Requires semgrep.yml in repo root (see that file) — payment-credential-logging
    # and unsanitized dangerouslySetInnerHTML taint/pattern rules, tested locally.
    semgrep:
      enabled: true
      config_file: "semgrep.yml"

  # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  # AUTO-REVIEW triggers
  # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  auto_review:
    enabled: true
    # Review every push to a PR, not just on open
    auto_incremental_review: true
    # Don't waste review on draft PRs
    drafts: false
    # Ignore PRs that are purely dependency updates
    ignore_title_keywords:
      - "chore(deps)"
      - "dependabot"

  # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  # PRE-MERGE CHECKS — actual merge-blocking gates (requires
  # request_changes_workflow: true above to enforce `error` mode).
  # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  pre_merge_checks:
    # Blunt repo-wide docstring % gate is intentionally OFF — it can't be
    # path-scoped, so it can't distinguish shared components/exported hooks
    # (which need JSDoc per components.md) from leaf components (which don't).
    # Replaced by the docstring-convention-compliance custom_check below.
    docstrings:
      mode: "off"
    title:
      mode: error
      requirements: >-
        Must follow Conventional Commits format: type(scope): description.
        Valid types: feat, fix, docs, style, refactor, perf, test, build, ci,
        chore, upstream-sync. Scope is optional but encouraged.
    description:
      mode: error
    # Jira Forge app is not yet installed in the Atlassian instance — this has
    # nothing to assess against until that connection exists. Flip to `error`
    # once installed (see knowledge_base.jira below).
    issue_assessment:
      mode: warning
    custom_checks:
      - name: "Docstring convention compliance"
        mode: error
        instructions: >-
          Fail this check only if the PR adds or modifies (a) a component consumed
          by 2 or more callers (a shared component per protectedFiles.md/components.md),
          (b) an exported hook under overrides/app/hooks/**, or (c) a utility function
          with non-obvious behaviour — and the added/modified declaration does not
          have a JSDoc comment (hooks must include a @returns description).
          Do NOT fail for: leaf/single-consumer components, trivial or self-evident
          utilities, type-only files, test files, or story files. Pass if no
          qualifying declaration was added or modified in this PR.

  # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  # FINISHING TOUCHES — on-demand generation via PR checkbox or
  # @coderabbitai command
  # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  finishing_touches:
    docstrings:
      enabled: true

# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# CHAT — allows developers to ask CodeRabbit questions in PR comments
# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
chat:
  auto_reply: true

# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# KNOWLEDGE BASE — external context sources
# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
knowledge_base:
  jira:
    # NOTE: this only scopes context once the Jira Forge app is installed and
    # connected via the Atlassian Marketplace — it does not establish that
    # connection itself. As of this config, the Forge app is NOT yet installed
    # in zimmermannworkboard.atlassian.net. Link a Jira issue by pasting its
    # URL into the PR description (no auto-detection from branch name).
    usage: enabled
    project_keys:
      - "SFCC"
  code_guidelines:
    # AGENTS.md is already covered by CodeRabbit's own default file patterns
    # (confirmed in docs) — listed explicitly anyway for visibility. The
    # .claude/rules/*.md files are NOT covered by any default pattern, and
    # AGENTS.md's markdown links to them are not resolved/followed by
    # CodeRabbit (it reads literal file content only), so without this they
    # would not be used as review criteria at all.
    enabled: true
    filePatterns:
      - "AGENTS.md"
      - files: ".claude/rules/conventions.md"
        applyTo: "overrides/**"
      - files: ".claude/rules/typescript.md"
        applyTo: "overrides/**"
      - files: ".claude/rules/css.md"
        applyTo: "overrides/**"
      - files: ".claude/rules/components.md"
        applyTo: "overrides/app/components/**,overrides/app/pages/**,overrides/app/hooks/**"
      - files: ".claude/rules/testing.md"
        applyTo: "overrides/**,e2e/**"
      - files: ".claude/rules/frozenFiles.md"
        applyTo: "**"
      - files: ".claude/rules/protectedFiles.md"
        applyTo: "**"

# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# CODE GENERATION — style guidance for finishing_touches.docstrings
# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
code_generation:
  docstrings:
    path_instructions:
      - path: "overrides/app/hooks/**"
        instructions: >-
          Every exported hook needs a JSDoc comment including a @returns
          description, per components.md > Hooks.
      - path: "overrides/app/components/**"
        instructions: >-
          Only generate JSDoc for components consumed by 2 or more callers
          (Tier 2 shared components per protectedFiles.md). Skip leaf,
          single-consumer components — components.md says the prop type is
          sufficient for those.

# CodeRabbit only runs Semgrep when this file exists in the repo root.
# Tested locally: python3 -m venv /tmp/semgrep-venv && /tmp/semgrep-venv/bin/pip install semgrep
#   /tmp/semgrep-venv/bin/semgrep scan --config semgrep.yml <file>
rules:
  - id: payment-credential-logged
    languages: [typescript]
    severity: ERROR
    message: >-
      Payment credential (card number, CVV, PIN) flows into a logging/telemetry sink.
      Per conventions.md, these must never appear in console.*, Sentry, or analytics calls.
    mode: taint
    pattern-sources:
      - pattern-either:
          - patterns:
              - pattern: function $FN(..., $VAR, ...) { ... }
              - metavariable-regex:
                  metavariable: $VAR
                  regex: (?i)(cardNumber|cvv|pin|cardNum|pan)
      - patterns:
          - pattern: const $VAR = ...
          - metavariable-regex:
              metavariable: $VAR
              regex: (?i)(cardNumber|cvv|pin|cardNum|pan)
    pattern-sinks:
      - pattern: console.$METHOD(...)
      - pattern: Sentry.$METHOD(...)

  - id: dangerously-set-inner-html-unsanitized
    languages: [typescript]
    severity: ERROR
    message: >-
      dangerouslySetInnerHTML used without an obvious sanitizer call (e.g. DOMPurify.sanitize) — XSS risk.
    patterns:
      - pattern: '<$TAG ... dangerouslySetInnerHTML={{ __html: $X }} ... />'
      - pattern-not: '<$TAG ... dangerouslySetInnerHTML={{ __html: $SANITIZER.sanitize(...) }} ... />'

1	# 02 — Contentful (CMS)
2	
3	## 1. Purpose and scope
4	
5	Contentful is the headless CMS for editorial content: homepage modules, promotional banners, lookbooks, campaign landing pages, size guide fallback content (primary size guide is the Measmerize overlay — PRD-053), footer, and editorial blocks on PLPs and PDPs. The storefront reads published content via the **Delivery API (CDA)** from both SSR and the browser, reads draft content via the **Preview API (CPA)** in editor sessions, and receives **publish webhooks** to clear the SSR cache.
6	
7	In scope:
8	
9	- Reading published content via the Delivery API
10	- Reading draft content via the Preview API in editor preview sessions
11	- Live preview in Contentful Studio
12	- Locale-specific content via Contentful's native localisation
13	- Contentful Studio Experiences — drag-and-drop page composition by editors
14	- Receiving publish webhooks to clear stale SSR cache entries
15	
16	Out of scope of this document:
17	
18	- Content type schema sync (managed in code via the Management API — see §2)
19	- Asset uploads and content editing in Contentful Studio
20	- Webhooks from Contentful to SFCC (none planned)
21	
22	**Content ownership.** SFCC owns all commerce data; Contentful owns editorial. On pages that mix both, editorial comes from Contentful and commerce data is resolved from SFCC. Product and category references in Contentful entries are authored via the Salesforce Commerce Cloud Connector app and resolved at render (HPC-001). Rows marked *pending* are unconfirmed (see §11).
23	
24	| Surface | SFCC owns | Contentful owns | Status |
25	|---|---|---|---|
26	| Homepage | Commerce data for embedded product refs | All modules — hero, banners, campaign blocks | Confirmed |
27	| Campaign landing pages | Commerce data for embedded product refs | Full page (Contentful Studio Experiences) | Confirmed |
28	| Lookbooks | Commerce data for shop-the-look refs | Imagery, layout, copy | Confirmed |
29	| Size guides | — | Fallback content only — primary size guide is the Measmerize overlay (PRD-053, confirmed 2026-06-19); Contentful serves size guide content only where no Measmerize data exists for a given product | Updated |
30	| Footer | — | All content | Confirmed |
31	| PLP / category | Category results, product tiles, facets, pagination, hero/banner and editorial rows (SFCC BM — SPR-03/04/64) | Contentful-authored editorial rows, if any | *Whether any PLP editorial comes from Contentful is pending* |
32	| PDP | Product attributes, price, inventory, variations, gallery | Marketing copy, editorial blocks, size guide fallback (primary size guide is Measmerize — PRD-053) | *Which blocks are Contentful vs SFCC Page Designer is pending* |
33	| Navigation / mega-menu | Category tree | Promotional tiles, if any | *Pending* |
34	| Product badges | Badge labels and taxonomy — managed in SFCC BM product attributes (PRD-005); clickable badges link to category/PLP. Contentful is not the source of badge content unless explicitly confirmed. | — | Confirmed |
35	
36	## 2. Content type management (build-time)
37	
38	Content type schemas are managed in code, not in the Contentful UI:
39	
40	- Schema definitions live in the PWA repo and are reviewed via pull request.
41	- A sync script (Management API) idempotently upserts content types into the target environment. The sync script is authored to be additive only — it never deletes a field from a live content type.
42	- Each content type pairs with a typed React component. TypeScript types match the Contentful field IDs exactly, so schema drift is caught at compile time.
43	
44	## 3. Browser-side architecture
45	
46	```
47	PWA (SSR layer, then CSR hydration)
48	        │
49	        ├──► Contentful Delivery API (CDA) — published content
50	        │        SSR fetches server-side; browser also uses CDA on
51	        │        post-hydration reads. Public token, safe in bundle.
52	        │
53	        ├──► Contentful Preview API (CPA) — draft content
54	        │        Editor preview only. Token held server-side in MRT;
55	        │        never reaches the browser. Requests proxied through
56	        │        an MRT preview endpoint.
57	        │
58	        ├──► Contentful Images API (images.ctfassets.net)
59	        │        srcset / sizes / avif|webp / quality parameters
60	        │
61	        └──◄  Publish webhook → MRT /webhooks/contentful
62	                 Clears affected SSR cache keys on entry publish.
63	                 HMAC-verified with a shared secret.
64	```
65	
66	- **SSR first.** Editorial content for SEO- and LCP-critical pages (homepage, PLP, PDP, campaign landings) is fetched server-side. The browser hydrates from the SSR payload — no CDA call on first paint.
67	- **GraphQL for composed pages.** Where a page assembles many entries the storefront uses the GraphQL Content API to fetch only the needed fields in one request. REST CDA is used for simpler reads.
68	- **Live preview.** When an editor opens preview in Contentful Studio, the storefront renders inside Studio's iframe. It detects the preview origin, switches to the CPA-backed MRT proxy, and refreshes on `postMessage` events from Studio.
69	- **Asset delivery.** Images come from `images.ctfassets.net`. The storefront generates `srcset`, `sizes`, AVIF with WebP fallback, and quality parameters per breakpoint.
70	
71	## 4. Authentication and credentials
72	
73	| Token | Where used | Sensitivity |
74	|---|---|---|
75	| Delivery API token (CDA) | Browser bundle and SSR | Public — read-only, scoped to one environment. Safe to embed. |
76	| Preview API token (CPA) | MRT preview proxy only | Semi-sensitive — exposes drafts. MRT environment variable. Never reaches the browser. |
77	| Management API token (CMA) | Build-time schema sync script | High. Held on the CI host only. Never embedded. |
78	| Webhook shared secret | MRT webhook receiver | High. Verifies HMAC on inbound publish webhooks. MRT environment variable. |
79	
80	Each environment has its own CDA, CPA, and webhook-secret values. The CMA token is per-Space and held only on the CI host.
81	
82	## 5. Data exchanged
83	
84	| Direction | Data | Mechanism |
85	|---|---|---|
86	| Storefront → Contentful | Content type ID, locale, filters, GraphQL query | CDA / Preview API HTTPS GET |
87	| Contentful → Storefront | JSON entries with resolved linked references | CDA / Preview API response |
88	| Contentful → Storefront (assets) | Image and video asset URLs | Images API |
89	| Contentful Studio ↔ PWA iframe | Live preview update events | Cross-origin `postMessage` |
90	| Contentful → MRT | Publish webhook with entry ID, content type, locale, environment | HTTPS POST with HMAC signature |
91	
92	No PII flows through Contentful.
93	
94	## 6. Performance and loading strategy
95	
96	- **SSR cache.** Contentful responses are cached at the SSR/edge layer — TTL 60 seconds with stale-while-revalidate. Publish webhooks clear the cache; the TTL is the fallback.
97	- **CDN rate limits.** Contentful allows 55 uncached requests per second per CDA token. The SSR cache absorbs almost all traffic so this limit is only a risk during burst republish events.
98	- **Images.** AVIF with WebP fallback via the Images API. Lazy loading on all below-the-fold images. The largest hero carries `fetchpriority="high"`.
99	- **Preconnect.** `images.ctfassets.net` is preconnected from the document head. `cdn.contentful.com` is not — first paint hydrates from SSR, so no browser CDA call is on the critical path.
100	- **Bundle weight.** The rich-text renderer is dynamically imported only on pages that use rich-text fields.
101	- **Field projection.** GraphQL queries select only the fields the component uses. REST queries use the `select` parameter where supported.
102	
103	## 7. Multi-region behaviour
104	
105	- A single Contentful Space serves all eight storefronts via Contentful's native locale model.
106	- The active locale is resolved from the URL prefix and passed as `locale=` on every CDA request. Eleven active locales: en-AU, en-US, en-GB, en (EU), fr, it, es, en-CH, en-HK, en-AE.
107	- Region-specific entries (banners, promotions, editorial that varies by site) are filtered at query time using the active SFCC site ID.
108	
109	## 8. Failure modes and graceful degradation
110	
111	| Failure | Behaviour |
112	|---|---|
113	| Contentful CDA unavailable | Page renders without editorial content. Editorial slots show empty; commerce data is never blocked on a CMS read. |
114	| Stale cached content after a publish | Tolerated within the 60-second TTL. The publish webhook normally clears affected entries in seconds; the TTL is the safety net if the webhook drops. |
115	| Preview API returns broken or unpublished refs | Editor preview only — render a placeholder. Production traffic never hits this path. |
116	| Asset (image) 404 | Show alt text and a graceful placeholder. |
117	| 429 rate limit on CDA | Exponential backoff and retry. The SSR cache makes this rare in practice. |
118	| Publish webhook fails HMAC verification | Reject and log. Storefront continues serving from cache; the TTL picks up the change. |
119	| Live preview iframe disconnects | Storefront silently returns to non-preview mode. |
120	
121	## 9. Security and privacy
122	
123	- The CDA token is read-only and scoped to one environment. Embedding in the bundle is safe per Contentful's published guidance.
124	- The CPA token is held server-side only and is never logged.
125	- The CMA token is held only on the CI host — never embedded, never in PR diffs.
126	- No PII is handled by Contentful.
127	
128	## 10. Open items requiring client confirmation
129	
130	1. **`regions` content-model field.** The working assumption is that region-specific entries are filtered by a `regions` field containing the relevant SFCC site IDs. Pending content-strategy and editor-workflow sign-off — this field affects how editors author content across all eight storefronts.
131	2. **SFCC vs Contentful content ownership on composed pages.** The principle is settled — SFCC owns all commerce data, Contentful owns editorial. Not yet confirmed is the split on composed pages: which editorial blocks appear on PDP and PLP, whether they are authored in SFCC Page Designer or Contentful, whether category landing pages are SFCC-routed or built in Contentful Studio Experiences, and whether the mega-menu includes Contentful-authored promotional tiles. The working assumption is in the ownership table in §1.
132	3. **Contentful Space and per-environment credentials.** Contentful to provide per-environment CDA token, CPA token, Space ID, environment ID, and webhook secret so the storefront can be tested against a real Contentful environment.
133

- Receiving publish webhooks to clear stale SSR cache entries

Out of scope of this document:

- Content type schema sync (managed in code via the Management API — see §2)
- Asset uploads and content editing in Contentful Studio
- Webhooks from Contentful to SFCC (none planned)

**Content ownership.** SFCC owns all commerce data; Contentful owns editorial. On pages that mix both, editorial comes from Contentful and commerce data is resolved from SFCC. Product and category references in Contentful entries are authored via the Salesforce Commerce Cloud Connector app and resolved at render (HPC-001). Rows marked *pending* are unconfirmed (see §11).

| Surface | SFCC owns | Contentful owns | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| Homepage | Commerce data for embedded product refs | All modules — hero, banners, campaign blocks | Confirmed |
| Campaign landing pages | Commerce data for embedded product refs | Full page (Contentful Studio Experiences) | Confirmed |
| Lookbooks | Commerce data for shop-the-look refs | Imagery, layout, copy | Confirmed |
| Size guides | — | Fallback content only — primary size guide is the Measmerize overlay (PRD-053, confirmed 2026-06-19); Contentful serves size guide content only where no Measmerize data exists for a given product | Updated |
| Footer | — | All content | Confirmed |
| PLP / category | Category results, product tiles, facets, pagination, hero/banner and editorial rows (SFCC BM — SPR-03/04/64) | Contentful-authored editorial rows, if any | *Whether any PLP editorial comes from Contentful is pending* |
| PDP | Product attributes, price, inventory, variations, gallery | Marketing copy, editorial blocks, size guide fallback (primary size guide is Measmerize — PRD-053) | *Which blocks are Contentful vs SFCC Page Designer is pending* |
| Navigation / mega-menu | Category tree | Promotional tiles, if any | *Pending* |
| Product badges | Badge labels and taxonomy — managed in SFCC BM product attributes (PRD-005); clickable badges link to category/PLP. Contentful is not the source of badge content unless explicitly confirmed. | — | Confirmed |

## 2. Content type management (build-time)

Content type schemas are managed in code, not in the Contentful UI:

- Schema definitions live in the PWA repo and are reviewed via pull request.
- A sync script (Management API) idempotently upserts content types into the target environment. The sync script is authored to be additive only — it never deletes a field from a live content type.
- Each content type pairs with a typed React component. TypeScript types match the Contentful field IDs exactly, so schema drift is caught at compile time.

## 3. Browser-side architecture

```
PWA (SSR layer, then CSR hydration)
        │
        ├──► Contentful Delivery API (CDA) — published content
        │        SSR fetches server-side; browser also uses CDA on
        │        post-hydration reads. Public token, safe in bundle.
        │
        ├──► Contentful Preview API (CPA) — draft content
        │        Editor preview only. Token held server-side in MRT;
        │        never reaches the browser. Requests proxied through
        │        an MRT preview endpoint.
        │
        ├──► Contentful Images API (images.ctfassets.net)
        │        srcset / sizes / avif|webp / quality parameters
        │
        └──◄  Publish webhook → MRT /webhooks/contentful
                 Clears affected SSR cache keys on entry publish.
                 HMAC-verified with a shared secret.
```

- **SSR first.** Editorial content for SEO- and LCP-critical pages (homepage, PLP, PDP, campaign landings) is fetched server-side. The browser hydrates from the SSR payload — no CDA call on first paint.
- **GraphQL for composed pages.** Where a page assembles many entries the storefront uses the GraphQL Content API to fetch only the needed fields in one request. REST CDA is used for simpler reads.
- **Live preview.** When an editor opens preview in Contentful Studio, the storefront renders inside Studio's iframe. It detects the preview origin, switches to the CPA-backed MRT proxy, and refreshes on `postMessage` events from Studio.
- **Asset delivery.** Images come from `images.ctfassets.net`. The storefront generates `srcset`, `sizes`, AVIF with WebP fallback, and quality parameters per breakpoint.

## 4. Authentication and credentials

| Token | Where used | Sensitivity |
|---|---|---|
| Delivery API token (CDA) | Browser bundle and SSR | Public — read-only, scoped to one environment. Safe to embed. |
| Preview API token (CPA) | MRT preview proxy only | Semi-sensitive — exposes drafts. MRT environment variable. Never reaches the browser. |
| Management API token (CMA) | Build-time schema sync script | High. Held on the CI host only. Never embedded. |
| Webhook shared secret | MRT webhook receiver | High. Verifies HMAC on inbound publish webhooks. MRT environment variable. |

Each environment has its own CDA, CPA, and webhook-secret values. The CMA token is per-Space and held only on the CI host.

## 5. Data exchanged

| Direction | Data | Mechanism |
|---|---|---|
| Storefront → Contentful | Content type ID, locale, filters, GraphQL query | CDA / Preview API HTTPS GET |
| Contentful → Storefront | JSON entries with resolved linked references | CDA / Preview API response |
| Contentful → Storefront (assets) | Image and video asset URLs | Images API |
| Contentful Studio ↔ PWA iframe | Live preview update events | Cross-origin `postMessage` |
| Contentful → MRT | Publish webhook with entry ID, content type, locale, environment | HTTPS POST with HMAC signature |

No PII flows through Contentful.

## 6. Performance and loading strategy

- **SSR cache.** Contentful responses are cached at the SSR/edge layer — TTL 60 seconds with stale-while-revalidate. Publish webhooks clear the cache; the TTL is the fallback.
- **CDN rate limits.** Contentful allows 55 uncached requests per second per CDA token. The SSR cache absorbs almost all traffic so this limit is only a risk during burst republish events.
- **Images.** AVIF with WebP fallback via the Images API. Lazy loading on all below-the-fold images. The largest hero carries `fetchpriority="high"`.
- **Preconnect.** `images.ctfassets.net` is preconnected from the document head. `cdn.contentful.com` is not — first paint hydrates from SSR, so no browser CDA call is on the critical path.
- **Bundle weight.** The rich-text renderer is dynamically imported only on pages that use rich-text fields.
- **Field projection.** GraphQL queries select only the fields the component uses. REST queries use the `select` parameter where supported.

## 7. Multi-region behaviour

- A single Contentful Space serves all eight storefronts via Contentful's native locale model.
- The active locale is resolved from the URL prefix and passed as `locale=` on every CDA request. Eleven active locales: en-AU, en-US, en-GB, en (EU), fr, it, es, en-CH, en-HK, en-AE.
- Region-specific entries (banners, promotions, editorial that varies by site) are filtered at query time using the active SFCC site ID.

## 8. Failure modes and graceful degradation

| Failure | Behaviour |
|---|---|
| Contentful CDA unavailable | Page renders without editorial content. Editorial slots show empty; commerce data is never blocked on a CMS read. |
| Stale cached content after a publish | Tolerated within the 60-second TTL. The publish webhook normally clears affected entries in seconds; the TTL is the safety net if the webhook drops. |
| Preview API returns broken or unpublished refs | Editor preview only — render a placeholder. Production traffic never hits this path. |
| Asset (image) 404 | Show alt text and a graceful placeholder. |
| 429 rate limit on CDA | Exponential backoff and retry. The SSR cache makes this rare in practice. |
| Publish webhook fails HMAC verification | Reject and log. Storefront continues serving from cache; the TTL picks up the change. |
| Live preview iframe disconnects | Storefront silently returns to non-preview mode. |

## 9. Security and privacy

- The CDA token is read-only and scoped to one environment. Embedding in the bundle is safe per Contentful's published guidance.
- The CPA token is held server-side only and is never logged.
- The CMA token is held only on the CI host — never embedded, never in PR diffs.
- No PII is handled by Contentful.

## 10. Open items requiring client confirmation

1. **`regions` content-model field.** The working assumption is that region-specific entries are filtered by a `regions` field containing the relevant SFCC site IDs. Pending content-strategy and editor-workflow sign-off — this field affects how editors author content across all eight storefronts.
2. **SFCC vs Contentful content ownership on composed pages.** The principle is settled — SFCC owns all commerce data, Contentful owns editorial. Not yet confirmed is the split on composed pages: which editorial blocks appear on PDP and PLP, whether they are authored in SFCC Page Designer or Contentful, whether category landing pages are SFCC-routed or built in Contentful Studio Experiences, and whether the mega-menu includes Contentful-authored promotional tiles. The working assumption is in the ownership table in §1.
3. **Contentful Space and per-environment credentials.** Contentful to provide per-environment CDA token, CPA token, Space ID, environment ID, and webhook secret so the storefront can be tested against a real Contentful environment.
