1	#!/bin/bash
2	# Pre-commit hook:
3	#   1. Regenerate the Claude Code registry and stage any changes.
4	#   2. If any Studio Experiences component (experiences/*.tsx) is staged,
5	#      regenerate definitions.ts and stage it automatically.
6	#   3. Protect derived configuration files from direct edits.
7	#   4. Block .env.sample commits that contain secret-class key values.
8	#
9	# Setup: hooks are managed by Husky v9 — run `npm install` and they are installed automatically.
10	#   Husky sets core.hooksPath to .husky/_ and .husky/pre-commit calls this script.
11	#   If you ever need to install manually (e.g. npm install --ignore-scripts):
12	#   cp scripts/hooks/pre-commit .git/hooks/pre-commit && chmod +x .git/hooks/pre-commit
13	#   cp scripts/hooks/commit-msg .git/hooks/commit-msg && chmod +x .git/hooks/commit-msg
14	
15	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
16	# 0. Ensure node is on PATH.
17	#    Git hooks run in a non-interactive shell — version managers (nvm, fnm,
18	#    volta) are not sourced automatically. Try each in turn; fail loudly if
19	#    node still can't be found so the developer knows what to fix.
20	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
21	
22	if ! command -v node &>/dev/null; then
23	  # nvm (most common on macOS)
24	  export NVM_DIR="${NVM_DIR:-$HOME/.nvm}"
25	  [ -s "$NVM_DIR/nvm.sh" ] && \. "$NVM_DIR/nvm.sh"
26	
27	  # fnm
28	  if ! command -v node &>/dev/null && command -v fnm &>/dev/null; then
29	    eval "$(fnm env 2>/dev/null || true)"
30	  fi
31	
32	  # volta
33	  if ! command -v node &>/dev/null; then
34	    export PATH="$HOME/.volta/bin:$PATH"
35	  fi
36	
37	  if ! command -v node &>/dev/null; then
38	    echo "  ❌  pre-commit: node not found. Make sure your version manager is"
39	    echo "      initialised (nvm, fnm, or volta) and node is installed."
40	    exit 1
41	  fi
42	fi
43	
44	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
45	# 1. Registry regeneration — runs on every commit to keep .claude/registry/
46	#    in sync. Stages any updated registry files automatically.
47	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
48	
49	staged=$(git diff --cached --name-only)
50	
51	registry_components=$(echo "$staged" | grep -E '^overrides/app/components/' || true)
52	registry_hooks=$(echo "$staged" | grep -E '^overrides/app/hooks/' || true)
53	registry_utils=$(echo "$staged" | grep -E '^overrides/app/utils/' || true)
54	registry_pages=$(echo "$staged" | grep -E '^overrides/app/pages/' || true)
55	registry_routes=$(echo "$staged" | grep -E '^overrides/app/routes\.(tsx|jsx)$' || true)
56	
57	if [ -n "$registry_components$registry_hooks$registry_utils$registry_pages$registry_routes" ] \
58	  && command -v node &>/dev/null && [ -f "scripts/generateRegistry.mjs" ]; then
59	  echo "Regenerating Claude Code registry..."
60	  node scripts/generateRegistry.mjs
61	  git add .claude/registry/
62	fi
63	
64	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
65	# 1b. AI rules sync — when a .claude/ source file is staged, auto-regenerate
66	#     the derived files (.cursor/rules/, .vscode/instructions/,
67	#     .github/copilot-instructions.md) and stage the updates. Only the "auto"
68	#     targets are regenerated; manual targets remain untouched.
69	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
70	
71	if command -v node &>/dev/null && [ -f "scripts/syncCursorRules.mjs" ]; then
72	  ai_sources_staged=$(git diff --cached --name-only \
73	    | grep -E '^\.claude/(rules/.*\.md|skills/.*/SKILL\.md)$' \
74	    || true)
75	
76	  if [ -n "$ai_sources_staged" ]; then
77	    echo "AI rule source(s) changed — running sync:ai-rules:fix..."
78	    if ! node scripts/syncCursorRules.mjs --fix > /dev/null; then
79	      echo ""
80	      echo "  ❌  sync:ai-rules:fix failed — derived AI config files may be stale or partially"
81	      echo "      written. Fix the error above, then re-stage and commit again."
82	      echo ""
83	      exit 1
84	    fi
85	    git add .cursor/rules/ .vscode/instructions/ .github/copilot-instructions.md 2>/dev/null || true
86	  fi
87	fi
88	
89	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
90	# 1c. Skill inventory sync reminder — when a skill is added, removed, or
91	#     changed, remind the developer to update .claude/skills/README.md (the
92	#     canonical skill reference) and the mirrored Confluence page. Warning
93	#     only — there is no Confluence API integration wired up to verify this
94	#     automatically.
95	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
96	
97	skill_files_staged=$(git diff --cached --name-only \
98	  | grep -E '^\.claude/skills/[^/]+/SKILL\.md$' \
99	  || true)
100	
101	if [ -n "$skill_files_staged" ]; then
102	  echo ""
103	  echo "Skill file(s) changed:"
104	  echo "$skill_files_staged" | sed 's/^/  - /'
105	
106	  if ! git diff --cached --name-only | grep -qF '.claude/skills/README.md'; then
107	    echo ""
108	    echo "  ⚠️  .claude/skills/README.md is not staged — update it to match"
109	    echo "     (see 'Adding a new skill' at the bottom of that file)."
110	  fi
111	
112	  echo ""
113	  echo "  ⚠️  Reminder: also update the mirrored Confluence page (child page under"
114	  echo "     page ID 297140226, \"Claude Code Skills Reference\") — there is no"
115	  echo "     automated push from this repo to Confluence yet."
116	  echo "  Committing anyway — this is a warning only."
117	  echo ""
118	fi
119	
120	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
121	# 2. Contentful Studio Experiences codegen
122	#    When any experiences/*.tsx file is staged, regenerate definitions.ts
123	#    and stage it automatically. Blocks the commit on codegen failure.
124	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
125	
126	experiences_staged=$(git diff --cached --name-only \
127	  | grep -E 'overrides/app/components/contentful/experiences/.*\.tsx$' \
128	  || true)
129	
130	if [ -n "$experiences_staged" ]; then
131	  echo "Studio Experiences component staged — regenerating definitions.ts..."
132	
133	  REAL_EXPERIENCES="overrides/app/components/contentful/experiences"
134	  tmp_exp=$(mktemp -d)
135	  trap 'rm -rf "$tmp_exp"' EXIT
136	
137	  # Populate temp dir with the staged version of each .tsx.
138	  # Files that are not staged are copied from the working tree so the generator
139	  # sees a complete set. definitions.ts is excluded — it is the output target.
140	  for f in "$REAL_EXPERIENCES"/*.tsx; do
141	    [[ -f "$f" ]] || continue
142	    name=$(basename "$f")
143	    [[ "$name" == "definitions.ts" ]] && continue
144	    if echo "$experiences_staged" | grep -qF "$f"; then
145	      git show ":0:$f" > "$tmp_exp/$name"
146	    else
147	      cp "$f" "$tmp_exp/$name"
148	    fi
149	  done
150	
151	  if ! CF_EXPERIENCES_DIR="$tmp_exp" node scripts/contentful/generateDefinitions.mjs; then
152	    echo ""
153	    echo "  ❌  Contentful codegen failed. Fix the errors above and try again."
154	    exit 1
155	  fi
156	
157	  cp "$tmp_exp/definitions.ts" "$REAL_EXPERIENCES/definitions.ts"
158	  git add "$REAL_EXPERIENCES/definitions.ts"
159	  echo "  ✓  definitions.ts updated and staged."
160	fi
161	
162	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
163	# 3. Derived configuration file guard
164	#    Blocks commits that directly edit derived files (.cursor/rules/,
165	#    .vscode/instructions/, .github/copilot-instructions.md) without also
166	#    staging the .claude/ source they were generated from.
167	#    Only triggers on MODIFIED files (diff-filter=M) — newly created derived
168	#    files are allowed through so the initial sync commit is not blocked.
169	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
170	
171	blocked_files=()
172	
173	# Get all MODIFIED (not newly added) staged files
174	modified_staged=$(git diff --cached --diff-filter=M --name-only || true)
175	
176	while IFS= read -r file; do
177	  [[ -z "$file" ]] && continue
178	
179	  # Only check files in derived locations
180	  case "$file" in
181	    .cursor/rules/*|.vscode/instructions/*|.github/copilot-instructions.md) ;;
182	    *) continue ;;
183	  esac
184	
185	  # Only check if the file exists and contains a synced-from comment
186	  [[ ! -f "$file" ]] && continue
187	  synced_line=$(grep -m1 'synced-from:' "$file" 2>/dev/null || true)
188	  [[ -z "$synced_line" ]] && continue
189	
190	  # Extract all source paths from the synced-from comment
191	  # Format: <!-- synced-from: path/to/source.md[, path2, ...] — ... -->
192	  synced_sources=$(echo "$synced_line" \
193	    | sed 's/.*synced-from:[[:space:]]*//' \
194	    | sed 's/[[:space:]]*—.*//')
195	
196	  [[ -z "$synced_sources" ]] && continue
197	
198	  # If ANY source is also staged in this commit, this is a legitimate sync
199	  # update — the developer edited a .claude/ source and ran the sync script.
200	  # Skip it.
201	  staged_names=$(git diff --cached --name-only)
202	  any_source_staged=false
203	  while IFS= read -r src; do
204	    src=$(echo "$src" | sed 's/^[[:space:]]*//;s/[[:space:]]*$//')
205	    [[ -z "$src" ]] && continue
206	    if echo "$staged_names" | grep -qxF -- "$src"; then
207	      any_source_staged=true
208	      break
209	    fi
210	  done <<< "$(echo "$synced_sources" | tr ',' '\n')"
211	  if $any_source_staged; then
212	    continue
213	  fi
214	
215	  # Fall back to the same AI-sources trigger condition step 1b uses to decide
216	  # whether to regenerate this file in the first place. A derived file's own
217	  # synced-from header may not yet list every source that legitimately feeds
218	  # it (e.g. a skill file added after the header was last written) — if step
219	  # 1b would have regenerated this file because a .claude/rules/*.md or
220	  # .claude/skills/*/SKILL.md file is staged, that is also a legitimate sync,
221	  # not a direct edit.
222	  if echo "$staged_names" | grep -qE '^\.claude/(rules/.*\.md|skills/.*/SKILL\.md)$'; then
223	    continue
224	  fi
225	
226	  # Source is NOT staged — this derived file was edited directly.
227	  blocked_files+=("$file")
228	
229	done <<< "$modified_staged"
230	
231	if [ "${#blocked_files[@]}" -gt 0 ]; then
232	  echo ""
233	  echo "  ❌  Commit blocked — derived configuration file(s) edited directly:"
234	  echo ""
235	  for bf in "${blocked_files[@]}"; do
236	    echo "       $bf"
237	  done
238	  echo ""
239	  echo "  These files are generated from .claude/ sources and must not be edited directly."
240	  echo ""
241	  echo "  To update auto-generated rules:"
242	  echo "    1. Edit the .claude/ source (see the synced-from comment at the top of the file)"
243	  echo "    2. Run: node scripts/syncCursorRules.mjs --fix"
244	  echo "    3. Commit the .claude/ source and the regenerated file together"
245	  echo ""
246	  echo "  To propose changes to .claude/ master files or sync rules:"
247	  echo "    Raise the request to the Tech Lead via #dev-team"
248	  echo ""
249	  exit 1
250	fi
251	
252	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
253	# 4. .env.sample secrets guard
254	#    Blocks commits where a secret-class key has a non-empty value, or where
255	#    a value matches a known credential pattern (JWT, long hex, base64, provider
256	#    prefixes). Runs only when .env.sample is staged.
257	#    Secret-class key names: *_SECRET, *_TOKEN, *_PASSWORD, *_CREDENTIAL,
258	#    *_PRIVATE_KEY, *_API_KEY, *_BEARER, *_SIGNING_KEY, *_ENCRYPTION_KEY,
259	#    *_DSN, *_WEBHOOK_SECRET.
260	#    Non-secret public identifiers (ORG_ID, SITE_ID, SHORT_CODE, CLIENT_ID,
261	#    SPACE_ID, ENVIRONMENT_ID, OCAPI_HOST) may keep placeholder values.
262	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
263	
264	if git diff --cached --name-only | grep -qF '.env.sample'; then
265	  secret_violations=()
266	
267	  while IFS= read -r line; do
268	    [[ "$line" =~ ^[[:space:]]*# ]] && continue
269	    [[ -z "${line// }" ]] && continue
270	    [[ "$line" =~ ^([A-Z_][A-Z0-9_]*)=(.*)$ ]] || continue
271	    key="${BASH_REMATCH[1]}"
272	    value="${BASH_REMATCH[2]}"
273	    [[ -z "$value" ]] && continue
274	
275	    # Secret-class key name with a non-empty value
276	    if echo "$key" | grep -qE '(_SECRET|_TOKEN|_PASSWORD|_CREDENTIAL|_PRIVATE_KEY|_API_KEY|_BEARER|_SIGNING_KEY|_ENCRYPTION_KEY|_DSN|_WEBHOOK_SECRET)'; then
277	      secret_violations+=("  $key  (secret-class key name with non-empty value)")
278	      continue
279	    fi
280	
281	    # Value looks like a JWT
282	    if echo "$value" | grep -qE '^eyJ[A-Za-z0-9_-]+\.[A-Za-z0-9_-]+\.[A-Za-z0-9_-]+$'; then
283	      secret_violations+=("  $key  (value looks like a JWT)")
284	      continue
285	    fi
286	
287	    # Value looks like a hex credential (32+ pure hex chars)
288	    if echo "$value" | grep -qE '^[0-9a-fA-F]{32,}$'; then
289	      secret_violations+=("  $key  (value looks like a hex credential)")
290	      continue
291	    fi
292	
293	    # Value looks like a base64 credential (40+ chars)
294	    if echo "$value" | grep -qE '^[A-Za-z0-9+/]{40,}={0,2}$'; then
295	      secret_violations+=("  $key  (value looks like a base64 credential)")
296	      continue
297	    fi
298	
299	    # Known provider-specific key prefixes
300	    if echo "$value" | grep -qE '^(AKIA[0-9A-Z]{16}|ghp_[A-Za-z0-9]{36}|ghs_[A-Za-z0-9]{36}|sk-[A-Za-z0-9]{32,}|xox[bpars]-[A-Za-z0-9-]+)'; then
301	      secret_violations+=("  $key  (value matches a known provider secret format)")
302	      continue
303	    fi
304	
305	  done < <(git show ":0:.env.sample" 2>/dev/null || true)
306	
307	  if [ "${#secret_violations[@]}" -gt 0 ]; then
308	    echo ""
309	    echo "  ❌  Commit blocked — .env.sample contains secret-class key(s) with non-empty values:"
310	    echo ""
311	    for v in "${secret_violations[@]}"; do
312	      echo "    $v"
313	    done
314	    echo ""
315	    echo "  .env.sample must only contain blank values for secret-class keys."
316	    echo "  Non-secret public identifiers (ORG_ID, SITE_ID, etc.) may keep their values."
317	    echo ""
318	    echo "  Remove the value(s) above, re-stage .env.sample, and commit again."
319	    echo ""
320	    exit 1
321	  fi
322	fi
323	
324	exit 0
325

#   2. If any Studio Experiences component (experiences/*.tsx) is staged,
#      regenerate definitions.ts and stage it automatically.
#   3. Protect derived configuration files from direct edits.
#   4. Block .env.sample commits that contain secret-class key values.
#
# Setup: hooks are managed by Husky v9 — run `npm install` and they are installed automatically.
#   Husky sets core.hooksPath to .husky/_ and .husky/pre-commit calls this script.
#   If you ever need to install manually (e.g. npm install --ignore-scripts):
#   cp scripts/hooks/pre-commit .git/hooks/pre-commit && chmod +x .git/hooks/pre-commit
#   cp scripts/hooks/commit-msg .git/hooks/commit-msg && chmod +x .git/hooks/commit-msg

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 0. Ensure node is on PATH.
#    Git hooks run in a non-interactive shell — version managers (nvm, fnm,
#    volta) are not sourced automatically. Try each in turn; fail loudly if
#    node still can't be found so the developer knows what to fix.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

if ! command -v node &>/dev/null; then
  # nvm (most common on macOS)
  export NVM_DIR="${NVM_DIR:-$HOME/.nvm}"
  [ -s "$NVM_DIR/nvm.sh" ] && \. "$NVM_DIR/nvm.sh"

  # fnm
  if ! command -v node &>/dev/null && command -v fnm &>/dev/null; then
    eval "$(fnm env 2>/dev/null || true)"
  fi

  # volta
  if ! command -v node &>/dev/null; then
    export PATH="$HOME/.volta/bin:$PATH"
  fi

  if ! command -v node &>/dev/null; then
    echo "  ❌  pre-commit: node not found. Make sure your version manager is"
    echo "      initialised (nvm, fnm, or volta) and node is installed."
    exit 1
  fi
fi

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 1. Registry regeneration — runs on every commit to keep .claude/registry/
#    in sync. Stages any updated registry files automatically.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

staged=$(git diff --cached --name-only)

registry_components=$(echo "$staged" | grep -E '^overrides/app/components/' || true)
registry_hooks=$(echo "$staged" | grep -E '^overrides/app/hooks/' || true)
registry_utils=$(echo "$staged" | grep -E '^overrides/app/utils/' || true)
registry_pages=$(echo "$staged" | grep -E '^overrides/app/pages/' || true)
registry_routes=$(echo "$staged" | grep -E '^overrides/app/routes\.(tsx|jsx)$' || true)

if [ -n "$registry_components$registry_hooks$registry_utils$registry_pages$registry_routes" ] \
  && command -v node &>/dev/null && [ -f "scripts/generateRegistry.mjs" ]; then
  echo "Regenerating Claude Code registry..."
  node scripts/generateRegistry.mjs
  git add .claude/registry/
fi

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 1b. AI rules sync — when a .claude/ source file is staged, auto-regenerate
#     the derived files (.cursor/rules/, .vscode/instructions/,
#     .github/copilot-instructions.md) and stage the updates. Only the "auto"
#     targets are regenerated; manual targets remain untouched.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

if command -v node &>/dev/null && [ -f "scripts/syncCursorRules.mjs" ]; then
  ai_sources_staged=$(git diff --cached --name-only \
    | grep -E '^\.claude/(rules/.*\.md|skills/.*/SKILL\.md)$' \
    || true)

  if [ -n "$ai_sources_staged" ]; then
    echo "AI rule source(s) changed — running sync:ai-rules:fix..."
    if ! node scripts/syncCursorRules.mjs --fix > /dev/null; then
      echo ""
      echo "  ❌  sync:ai-rules:fix failed — derived AI config files may be stale or partially"
      echo "      written. Fix the error above, then re-stage and commit again."
      echo ""
      exit 1
    fi
    git add .cursor/rules/ .vscode/instructions/ .github/copilot-instructions.md 2>/dev/null || true
  fi
fi

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 1c. Skill inventory sync reminder — when a skill is added, removed, or
#     changed, remind the developer to update .claude/skills/README.md (the
#     canonical skill reference) and the mirrored Confluence page. Warning
#     only — there is no Confluence API integration wired up to verify this
#     automatically.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

skill_files_staged=$(git diff --cached --name-only \
  | grep -E '^\.claude/skills/[^/]+/SKILL\.md$' \
  || true)

if [ -n "$skill_files_staged" ]; then
  echo ""
  echo "Skill file(s) changed:"
  echo "$skill_files_staged" | sed 's/^/  - /'

  if ! git diff --cached --name-only | grep -qF '.claude/skills/README.md'; then
    echo ""
    echo "  ⚠️  .claude/skills/README.md is not staged — update it to match"
    echo "     (see 'Adding a new skill' at the bottom of that file)."
  fi

  echo ""
  echo "  ⚠️  Reminder: also update the mirrored Confluence page (child page under"
  echo "     page ID 297140226, \"Claude Code Skills Reference\") — there is no"
  echo "     automated push from this repo to Confluence yet."
  echo "  Committing anyway — this is a warning only."
  echo ""
fi

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 2. Contentful Studio Experiences codegen
#    When any experiences/*.tsx file is staged, regenerate definitions.ts
#    and stage it automatically. Blocks the commit on codegen failure.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

experiences_staged=$(git diff --cached --name-only \
  | grep -E 'overrides/app/components/contentful/experiences/.*\.tsx$' \
  || true)

if [ -n "$experiences_staged" ]; then
  echo "Studio Experiences component staged — regenerating definitions.ts..."

  REAL_EXPERIENCES="overrides/app/components/contentful/experiences"
  tmp_exp=$(mktemp -d)
  trap 'rm -rf "$tmp_exp"' EXIT

  # Populate temp dir with the staged version of each .tsx.
  # Files that are not staged are copied from the working tree so the generator
  # sees a complete set. definitions.ts is excluded — it is the output target.
  for f in "$REAL_EXPERIENCES"/*.tsx; do
    [[ -f "$f" ]] || continue
    name=$(basename "$f")
    [[ "$name" == "definitions.ts" ]] && continue
    if echo "$experiences_staged" | grep -qF "$f"; then
      git show ":0:$f" > "$tmp_exp/$name"
    else
      cp "$f" "$tmp_exp/$name"
    fi
  done

  if ! CF_EXPERIENCES_DIR="$tmp_exp" node scripts/contentful/generateDefinitions.mjs; then
    echo ""
    echo "  ❌  Contentful codegen failed. Fix the errors above and try again."
    exit 1
  fi

  cp "$tmp_exp/definitions.ts" "$REAL_EXPERIENCES/definitions.ts"
  git add "$REAL_EXPERIENCES/definitions.ts"
  echo "  ✓  definitions.ts updated and staged."
fi

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 3. Derived configuration file guard
#    Blocks commits that directly edit derived files (.cursor/rules/,
#    .vscode/instructions/, .github/copilot-instructions.md) without also
#    staging the .claude/ source they were generated from.
#    Only triggers on MODIFIED files (diff-filter=M) — newly created derived
#    files are allowed through so the initial sync commit is not blocked.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

blocked_files=()

# Get all MODIFIED (not newly added) staged files
modified_staged=$(git diff --cached --diff-filter=M --name-only || true)

while IFS= read -r file; do
  [[ -z "$file" ]] && continue

  # Only check files in derived locations
  case "$file" in
    .cursor/rules/*|.vscode/instructions/*|.github/copilot-instructions.md) ;;
    *) continue ;;
  esac

  # Only check if the file exists and contains a synced-from comment
  [[ ! -f "$file" ]] && continue
  synced_line=$(grep -m1 'synced-from:' "$file" 2>/dev/null || true)
  [[ -z "$synced_line" ]] && continue

  # Extract all source paths from the synced-from comment
  # Format: <!-- synced-from: path/to/source.md[, path2, ...] — ... -->
  synced_sources=$(echo "$synced_line" \
    | sed 's/.*synced-from:[[:space:]]*//' \
    | sed 's/[[:space:]]*—.*//')

  [[ -z "$synced_sources" ]] && continue

  # If ANY source is also staged in this commit, this is a legitimate sync
  # update — the developer edited a .claude/ source and ran the sync script.
  # Skip it.
  staged_names=$(git diff --cached --name-only)
  any_source_staged=false
  while IFS= read -r src; do
    src=$(echo "$src" | sed 's/^[[:space:]]*//;s/[[:space:]]*$//')
    [[ -z "$src" ]] && continue
    if echo "$staged_names" | grep -qxF -- "$src"; then
      any_source_staged=true
      break
    fi
  done <<< "$(echo "$synced_sources" | tr ',' '\n')"
  if $any_source_staged; then
    continue
  fi

  # Fall back to the same AI-sources trigger condition step 1b uses to decide
  # whether to regenerate this file in the first place. A derived file's own
  # synced-from header may not yet list every source that legitimately feeds
  # it (e.g. a skill file added after the header was last written) — if step
  # 1b would have regenerated this file because a .claude/rules/*.md or
  # .claude/skills/*/SKILL.md file is staged, that is also a legitimate sync,
  # not a direct edit.
  if echo "$staged_names" | grep -qE '^\.claude/(rules/.*\.md|skills/.*/SKILL\.md)$'; then
    continue
  fi

  # Source is NOT staged — this derived file was edited directly.
  blocked_files+=("$file")

done <<< "$modified_staged"

if [ "${#blocked_files[@]}" -gt 0 ]; then
  echo ""
  echo "  ❌  Commit blocked — derived configuration file(s) edited directly:"
  echo ""
  for bf in "${blocked_files[@]}"; do
    echo "       $bf"
  done
  echo ""
  echo "  These files are generated from .claude/ sources and must not be edited directly."
  echo ""
  echo "  To update auto-generated rules:"
  echo "    1. Edit the .claude/ source (see the synced-from comment at the top of the file)"
  echo "    2. Run: node scripts/syncCursorRules.mjs --fix"
  echo "    3. Commit the .claude/ source and the regenerated file together"
  echo ""
  echo "  To propose changes to .claude/ master files or sync rules:"
  echo "    Raise the request to the Tech Lead via #dev-team"
  echo ""
  exit 1
fi

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 4. .env.sample secrets guard
#    Blocks commits where a secret-class key has a non-empty value, or where
#    a value matches a known credential pattern (JWT, long hex, base64, provider
#    prefixes). Runs only when .env.sample is staged.
#    Secret-class key names: *_SECRET, *_TOKEN, *_PASSWORD, *_CREDENTIAL,
#    *_PRIVATE_KEY, *_API_KEY, *_BEARER, *_SIGNING_KEY, *_ENCRYPTION_KEY,
#    *_DSN, *_WEBHOOK_SECRET.
#    Non-secret public identifiers (ORG_ID, SITE_ID, SHORT_CODE, CLIENT_ID,
#    SPACE_ID, ENVIRONMENT_ID, OCAPI_HOST) may keep placeholder values.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

if git diff --cached --name-only | grep -qF '.env.sample'; then
  secret_violations=()

  while IFS= read -r line; do
    [[ "$line" =~ ^[[:space:]]*# ]] && continue
    [[ -z "${line// }" ]] && continue
    [[ "$line" =~ ^([A-Z_][A-Z0-9_]*)=(.*)$ ]] || continue
    key="${BASH_REMATCH[1]}"
    value="${BASH_REMATCH[2]}"
    [[ -z "$value" ]] && continue

    # Secret-class key name with a non-empty value
    if echo "$key" | grep -qE '(_SECRET|_TOKEN|_PASSWORD|_CREDENTIAL|_PRIVATE_KEY|_API_KEY|_BEARER|_SIGNING_KEY|_ENCRYPTION_KEY|_DSN|_WEBHOOK_SECRET)'; then
      secret_violations+=("  $key  (secret-class key name with non-empty value)")
      continue
    fi

    # Value looks like a JWT
    if echo "$value" | grep -qE '^eyJ[A-Za-z0-9_-]+\.[A-Za-z0-9_-]+\.[A-Za-z0-9_-]+$'; then
      secret_violations+=("  $key  (value looks like a JWT)")
      continue
    fi

    # Value looks like a hex credential (32+ pure hex chars)
    if echo "$value" | grep -qE '^[0-9a-fA-F]{32,}$'; then
      secret_violations+=("  $key  (value looks like a hex credential)")
      continue
    fi

    # Value looks like a base64 credential (40+ chars)
    if echo "$value" | grep -qE '^[A-Za-z0-9+/]{40,}={0,2}$'; then
      secret_violations+=("  $key  (value looks like a base64 credential)")
      continue
    fi

    # Known provider-specific key prefixes
    if echo "$value" | grep -qE '^(AKIA[0-9A-Z]{16}|ghp_[A-Za-z0-9]{36}|ghs_[A-Za-z0-9]{36}|sk-[A-Za-z0-9]{32,}|xox[bpars]-[A-Za-z0-9-]+)'; then
      secret_violations+=("  $key  (value matches a known provider secret format)")
      continue
    fi

  done < <(git show ":0:.env.sample" 2>/dev/null || true)

  if [ "${#secret_violations[@]}" -gt 0 ]; then
    echo ""
    echo "  ❌  Commit blocked — .env.sample contains secret-class key(s) with non-empty values:"
    echo ""
    for v in "${secret_violations[@]}"; do
      echo "    $v"
    done
    echo ""
    echo "  .env.sample must only contain blank values for secret-class keys."
    echo "  Non-secret public identifiers (ORG_ID, SITE_ID, etc.) may keep their values."
    echo ""
    echo "  Remove the value(s) above, re-stage .env.sample, and commit again."
    echo ""
    exit 1
  fi
fi

exit 0

name: Protected File Guard

# Server-side enforcement of the tier/squad model. The client-side
# .claude/hooks/tier2Warn.sh is non-blocking — this workflow is the
# authoritative gate at PR time.

on:
  pull_request:
    branches:
      - develop
      - main
      - 'release/**'
    types: [opened, synchronize, reopened]

jobs:
  # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  # JOB 1 — Warning (non-blocking): Tier 1 files touched.
  # NOT a required status check (see AGENTS.md > Tier 1 Approval for why).
  # The actual hard block is CODEOWNERS + require_code_owner_reviews on
  # branch protection, enforced natively by GitHub with no Actions
  # involvement. This job exists to post the loud, informative warning and
  # owner-contact-map — useful context, not the gate itself.
  #
  # History: this used to be a required check with a second job
  # (tier1-guard-recheck) that re-evaluated it on every review submission
  # via the Checks API, so it could flip from fail to pass without a new
  # commit. That approach stopped working once GitHub locked down check-run
  # updates to same-run-only in Feb 2025 (see
  # https://github.blog/changelog/2025-02-12-notice-of-upcoming-deprecations-and-breaking-changes-for-github-actions/#changes-to-check-run-status-modification) —
  # a different workflow run can no longer flip another run's check
  # conclusion. Since a single pull_request-triggered run can't wait around
  # for a future review, and re-running the whole job on review events just
  # creates a second, stale-vs-fresh check-run record under the same name
  # (which GitHub does NOT treat the newer one as superseding for
  # merge-blocking purposes), there's no way to make this job itself both
  # required and reliably self-updating. CODEOWNERS already does this
  # correctly and natively, so that's the real gate.
  # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  tier1-guard:
    name: "🔴 Tier 1 — Frozen Files Check"
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: read
      pull-requests: read
    steps:
      - name: Checkout
        uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0
          ref: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}

      - name: Get changed files
        id: changed
        uses: tj-actions/changed-files@2d756ea4c53f7f6b397767d8723b3a10a9f35bf2 # v44
        with:
          base_sha: ${{ github.event.pull_request.base.sha }}
          sha: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}
          files_yaml: |
            tier1:
              # Design tokens — owner: UI Designer
              - 'overrides/app/theme/foundation/**'
              - 'overrides/app/theme/index.ts'
              # Commerce SDK hooks (overrides surface) — owner: Integration Lead
              - 'overrides/app/hooks/use-current-basket.*'
              - 'overrides/app/hooks/use-current-customer.*'
              - 'overrides/app/hooks/use-einstein.*'
              - 'overrides/app/hooks/use-datacloud.*'
              - 'overrides/app/hooks/use-refresh-token.*'
              - 'overrides/app/hooks/use-multi-site.*'
              - 'overrides/app/hooks/use-navigation.*'
              # Runtime & integration config — owner: Integration Lead
              - 'config/**'
              - 'overrides/app/ssr.*'
              - 'worker/main.*'
              - 'mobify.config.js'
              - 'package.json'
              - 'package-lock.json'
              # Test & tooling config — owner: Integration Lead
              - 'vitest.config.*'
              - 'playwright.config.*'
              - '.storybook/**'
              - 'tests/lighthouserc.*'
              - 'lighthouserc.*'
              # CI/CD — owner: Integration Lead
              - '.github/workflows/**'
              # Governance — owner: Both Squad Leads + Integration Lead
              - 'AGENTS.md'
              - 'CLAUDE.md'
              - 'CODEOWNERS'
              - '.claude/rules/**'
              - '.claude/settings.json'
              - 'coderabbit.yaml'
              - '.coderabbit/**'
              - 'semgrep.yml'
              - 'scripts/hooks/**'

      - name: Warn if Tier 1 files changed (informational — not a merge block)
        if: steps.changed.outputs.tier1_any_changed == 'true'
        run: |
          echo ""
          echo "━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━"
          echo "🔴 TIER 1 PROTECTED FILES DETECTED IN THIS PR"
          echo "━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━"
          echo ""
          echo "The following frozen files have been modified:"
          echo ""
          echo "${{ steps.changed.outputs.tier1_all_changed_files }}" | tr ' ' '\n' | sed 's/^/  ❌ /'
          echo ""
          echo "These files require an approving code-owner review before merge."
          echo "This check is informational — the actual merge block is CODEOWNERS +"
          echo "the required code-owner review, enforced by GitHub natively."
          echo ""
          echo "REQUIRED ACTIONS before this PR can be merged:"
          echo "  1. Get an approving review (not just a comment) from a member of"
          echo "     @ZimmermannAU/tier-1-approvers — CODEOWNERS auto-requests this."
          echo "  2. Contact the correct owner using the table below"
          echo ""
          echo "OWNER CONTACT MAP:"
          echo "  overrides/app/theme/foundation/      → UI Designer      (#design-system)"
          echo "  overrides/app/theme/index.ts         → UI Designer      (#design-system)"
          echo "  overrides/app/hooks/use-current-*   → Integration Lead (#integration)"
          echo "  overrides/app/hooks/use-einstein    → Integration Lead (#integration)"
          echo "  overrides/app/hooks/use-datacloud   → Integration Lead (#integration)"
          echo "  overrides/app/hooks/use-refresh-tok → Integration Lead (#integration)"
          echo "  overrides/app/hooks/use-multi-site  → Integration Lead (#integration)"
          echo "  overrides/app/hooks/use-navigation  → Integration Lead (#integration)"
          echo "  config/                             → Integration Lead (#integration)"
          echo "  overrides/app/ssr.*                 → Integration Lead (#integration)"
          echo "  worker/main.*                       → Integration Lead (#integration)"
          echo "  mobify.config.js                    → Integration Lead (#integration)"
          echo "  package.json (root)                 → Integration Lead (#integration)"
          echo "  vitest/playwright/.storybook config → Integration Lead (#integration)"
          echo "  .github/workflows/                  → Integration Lead (#integration)"
          echo "  AGENTS.md / CLAUDE.md / CODEOWNERS  → Both Squad Leads + Integration Lead (#dev-team)"
          echo "  .claude/rules/ / .claude/settings   → Both Squad Leads + Integration Lead (#dev-team)"
          echo "  coderabbit.yaml / .coderabbit/      → Both Squad Leads + Integration Lead (#dev-team)"
          echo "  semgrep.yml / scripts/hooks/        → Both Squad Leads + Integration Lead (#dev-team)"
          echo ""
          echo "━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━"

      - name: Pass — no Tier 1 files changed
        if: steps.changed.outputs.tier1_any_changed == 'false'
        run: |
          echo "✅ No Tier 1 protected files detected in this PR."

  # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  # JOB 2 — Hard block: PR targeting wrong branch
  # Prevents direct PRs to main that bypass develop
  # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  branch-target-guard:
    name: "🔴 Branch Target Check"
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:
      - name: Block direct PRs to main from feature branches
        run: |
          BASE="${{ github.base_ref }}"
          HEAD="${{ github.head_ref }}"

          echo "Base branch: $BASE"
          echo "Head branch: $HEAD"

          # Feature branches must not go directly to main
          if [[ "$BASE" == "main" && "$HEAD" == feature/* ]]; then
            echo ""
            echo "━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━"
            echo "🔴 INVALID BRANCH TARGET"
            echo "━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━"
            echo ""
            echo "Feature branches must target 'develop', not 'main'."
            echo ""
            echo "Correct flow: feature/* → develop → (release/*) → main"
            echo ""
            echo "Please update the base branch of this PR to 'develop'."
            echo "━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━"
            exit 1
          fi

          echo "✅ Branch target is valid."

  # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  # JOB 3 — Warning (non-blocking): Tier 2 files touched
  # Posts a PR comment listing Tier 2 files and required reviewers
  # Does NOT fail the build — but CodeRabbit will escalate review
  # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  tier2-warning:
    name: "🟡 Tier 2 — Protected Files Warning"
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      pull-requests: write
      contents: read
    steps:
      - name: Checkout
        uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0

      - name: Get changed Tier 2 files
        id: changed
        uses: tj-actions/changed-files@2d756ea4c53f7f6b397767d8723b3a10a9f35bf2 # v44
        with:
          files_yaml: |
            tier2:
              # Global shell — both squads
              - 'overrides/app/components/header/**'
              - 'overrides/app/components/footer/**'
              - 'overrides/app/components/drawer-menu/**'
              - 'overrides/app/components/list-menu/**'
              - 'overrides/app/components/seo/**'
              - 'overrides/app/components/_app/**'
              - 'overrides/app/components/_app-config/**'
              - 'overrides/app/routes.*'
              # Shared product components — Squad B primary, Squad A notified
              - 'overrides/app/components/product-tile/**'
              - 'overrides/app/components/product-item/**'
              - 'overrides/app/components/display-price/**'
              - 'overrides/app/components/image-gallery/**'
              - 'overrides/app/components/swatch-group/**'
              - 'overrides/app/components/recommended-products/**'
              # Shared commerce components — Squad A primary, Squad B notified
              - 'overrides/app/components/order-summary/**'
              - 'overrides/app/components/promo-code/**'
              - 'overrides/app/components/pickup-or-delivery/**'
              # Theme component styles — UI Designer
              - 'overrides/app/theme/components/**'
              # Translations — Integration / SI Partner
              - 'translations/**'
              - 'overrides/app/static/translations/**'
              # Shared hooks — both squads
              - 'overrides/app/hooks/use-auth-modal.*'
              - 'overrides/app/hooks/use-toast.*'
              - 'overrides/app/hooks/use-modal-state.*'
              - 'overrides/app/hooks/use-intersection-observer.*'
              - 'overrides/app/hooks/use-currency.*'
              - 'overrides/app/hooks/use-dnt-notification.*'
              - 'overrides/app/hooks/use-app-origin.*'
              - 'overrides/app/hooks/use-selected-store.*'

      - name: Post Tier 2 warning comment on PR
        if: steps.changed.outputs.tier2_any_changed == 'true'
        uses: actions/github-script@v7
        with:
          script: |
            const files = `${{ steps.changed.outputs.tier2_all_changed_files }}`
              .split(' ')
              .filter(Boolean)
              .map(f => `- \`${f}\``)
              .join('\n');

            const body = `## 🟡 Tier 2 Protected Files Detected

            This PR modifies shared components or hooks that are used across multiple features or squads.
            This is **not a merge block** — but it requires a second-developer review before merging.

            **Files affected:**
            ${files}

            **Required before merge:**
            - [ ] A developer from the **other squad** (not the PR author's squad) has reviewed and approved
            - [ ] The UI Designer has been notified if \`overrides/app/theme/components/\` is included
            - [ ] The Integration / SI Partner has been notified if \`translations/\` is included
            - [ ] No prop signature or export changes have been made without updating all consumers

            **Why this matters:** These files are imported by components in both Squad A and Squad B.
            A breaking change here — even a small one — will affect both squads simultaneously.

            _This comment is auto-generated by the Protected File Guard workflow._`;

            // Check if we already posted this comment to avoid duplicates
            const comments = await github.rest.issues.listComments({
              owner: context.repo.owner,
              repo: context.repo.repo,
              issue_number: context.issue.number,
            });

            const existing = comments.data.find(c =>
              c.body.includes('Tier 2 Protected Files Detected') &&
              c.user.login === 'github-actions[bot]'
            );

            if (existing) {
              await github.rest.issues.updateComment({
                owner: context.repo.owner,
                repo: context.repo.repo,
                comment_id: existing.id,
                body,
              });
            } else {
              await github.rest.issues.createComment({
                owner: context.repo.owner,
                repo: context.repo.repo,
                issue_number: context.issue.number,
                body,
              });
            }

      - name: Pass — no Tier 2 files changed
        if: steps.changed.outputs.tier2_any_changed == 'false'
        run: |
          echo "✅ No Tier 2 protected files detected in this PR."

  # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  # JOB 4 — Cross-squad boundary detection
  # Warns when a PR touches both Squad A and Squad B territory
  # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  cross-squad-guard:
    name: "🟡 Cross-Squad Boundary Check"
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      pull-requests: write
      contents: read
    steps:
      - name: Checkout
        uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0

      - name: Detect Squad A files changed
        id: squad-a
        uses: tj-actions/changed-files@2d756ea4c53f7f6b397767d8723b3a10a9f35bf2 # v44
        with:
          files_yaml: |
            squad_a:
              - 'overrides/app/pages/cart/**'
              - 'overrides/app/pages/checkout/**'
              - 'overrides/app/pages/checkout-one-click/**'
              - 'overrides/app/pages/confirmation/**'

              - 'overrides/app/components/bonus-product-view-modal/**'
              - 'overrides/app/hooks/use-checkout-auto-select.*'
              - 'overrides/app/hooks/use-multiship.*'
              - 'overrides/app/hooks/use-pickup-shipment.*'
              - 'overrides/app/hooks/use-sf-payments.*'

      - name: Detect Squad B files changed
        id: squad-b
        uses: tj-actions/changed-files@2d756ea4c53f7f6b397767d8723b3a10a9f35bf2 # v44
        with:
          files_yaml: |
            squad_b:
              - 'overrides/app/pages/home/**'
              - 'overrides/app/pages/product-detail/**'
              - 'overrides/app/pages/product-list/**'
              - 'overrides/app/pages/search/**'
              - 'overrides/app/pages/account/**'

content.text:
I now have everything needed, and the key facts are confirmed. Here's the grounded review.

---

# PR #41 Review — `feat(contentful): add Contentful Live Preview route`

## 🔴 Verdict: **REQUEST CHANGES**

The feature is well-built at the React level, but it **contradicts the confirmed integration doc's security architecture** and ships an ungated public preview route. Neither should merge silently. Details, severity-ordered and grounded.

**Current review state (for context):** CodeRabbit auto-**approved**, but its run reported "No actionable comments" on the **CHILL** profile — and critically, its `code_guidelines.filePatterns` (coderabbit.yaml:460–475) load `AGENTS.md` + `.claude/rules/**` but **not `.docs/integration/**`**, so it had no basis to catch the doc contradiction below. The only human comment (`TimLavelleACC`) is `@coderabbitai please review` — i.e. **no substantive human review yet**, and `reviewDecision: REVIEW_REQUIRED`.

---

## Blockers (must resolve before merge)

### B1 — Preview (CPA) token is shipped to the browser; contradicts `02-contentful.md` §3/§4/§9 🔴
This is the headline. The confirmed integration doc states the preview-token rule **four times**:
- §3 (line 53–56): *"Contentful Preview API (CPA) — draft content. Editor preview only. **Token held server-side in MRT; never reaches the browser. Requests proxied through an MRT preview endpoint.**"*
- §4 (line 76): CPA token → *"MRT preview proxy only … **Never reaches the browser.**"*
- §9 (line 124): *"The CPA token is **held server-side only**."*

What the PR actually does, in **client-side React page components**:
```ts
// contentfulPreview/index.tsx + experience/index.tsx
const token = previewAccessToken || accessToken
createClient({ accessToken: token, host: previewAccessToken ? 'preview.contentful.com' : 'cdn.contentful.com' })
```
I confirmed the token genuinely reaches the client: `config/default.js:186–190` puts `previewAccessToken: process.env.CONTENTFUL_PREVIEW_TOKEN` in the **same `app.contentful` object** as the (intentionally public) delivery token, with **no `ssrOnly` scoping** — and `contentful.ts:4–8` documents that this object is *"serialized into the bundle… available client-side."* So on any environment where `CONTENTFUL_PREVIEW_TOKEN` is set (exactly the local/staging/UAT envs where preview is used), the semi-sensitive CPA token is in the browser bundle and the browser calls `preview.contentful.com` directly — **not** the documented MRT proxy. This is precisely the risk `frozenFiles.md` flags on `contentful.ts` ("removing the server-side check exposes drafts").

Note also `experience/index.tsx` builds the client from `previewAccessToken || accessToken` **regardless of `?preview`** (the `isPreview` flag only toggles the `LivePreviewProvider` wrapper) — so on a preview-token-configured env, the *normal* `/:slug` route already serves draft content to all visitors via the exposed token.

**Fairness:** the token-in-browser pattern is partly **pre-existing** in `experience/index.tsx`. But this is the PR that turns preview into a shipped feature and adds a dedicated `/preview` entry point, so it's the right (and necessary) place to reconcile it. Per AGENTS.md *Doc integrity*, you can't merge code that contradicts a confirmed integration doc silently — either **(a)** implement the MRT preview proxy as documented (token server-side, browser → MRT endpoint), or **(b)** if the team has consciously chosen client-side live preview (plausible given the Contentful Studio licence question — see process note), **update §3/§4/§9 and get security sign-off** first.

### B2 — New public `/preview` route is ungated on prod + no `noindex` 🔴
`routes.tsx` registers `/preview` unconditionally with SSR enabled and no production gate. Doc §8 (line 115) is explicit: preview is *"Editor preview only… **Production traffic never hits this path.**"* As written, `/preview?entry=<id>` is a public, SSR-rendered, **crawlable** endpoint on production that renders arbitrary Experience entries by ID outside normal routing — and the repo's own CodeRabbit instruction for `overrides/app/routes.tsx` (coderabbit.yaml:245–255, Tier 2) says to check exactly these SEO/SSR implications. The `<Seo>` component is used elsewhere (`pages/home/index.tsx:217`) but neither preview path sets `noindex`. Gate the route out of production (or 404 when no preview token / not a preview env) and add `noindex`.

### B3 — Unrelated `.mcp.json` change bundled in (scope + supply-chain) 🟠
The PR adds a project-scoped MCP server:
```json
"b2c-dx-mcp": { "command": "npx", "args": ["-y", "@salesforce/b2c-dx-mcp@latest", "--allow-non-ga-tools"] }
```
This is unrelated to Contentful preview and rides along silently. Concerns: `@latest` is **unpinned** (every teammate's session auto-pulls whatever's newest — no reproducibility), `-y` auto-installs, and `--allow-non-ga-tools` enables **non-GA/experimental** tooling against B2C instances — project-wide, for everyone who opens the repo. It's *not* mechanically Tier 1 (the guard in `protected-file-guard.yml:86–95` lists `.claude/settings.json`, not `.mcp.json`), but it's governance-adjacent shared tooling. **Split it into its own PR** with integration-team awareness, and pin the version.

---

## Should-fix (quality — grounded in `.claude/rules/`)

- **`console.log` in a prod-shipped file** — `contentfulPreview/index.tsx` logs the detected type/locale. message.content: for #1 - isn't handing to the browser the main resolve to add Contentful Live Preview to the storefront — so content editors can see their Contentful edits rendered in the real storefront before publishing?

content.text:
Great question — and you're half right, which is exactly what makes it worth pulling apart. The short version: **live preview is a browser feature, but the *token* doesn't have to be in the browser to deliver it.** Those are two different things that the PR bundles together.

Let me use the backstage-pass analogy again.

There are actually **three moving parts** to Live Preview, and only one of them touches the token:

1. **The live magic** — editor types in Contentful Studio, and it shows up in the storefront instantly. This works because Studio (the parent window) **shouts the changed content over the wall** to the storefront iframe via `postMessage`. The browser gets the draft edits *directly from the editor's window* — **no Contentful API call, no token needed.** This genuinely must be client-side, and it is. ✅

2. **Inspector mode** — the clickable "edit this" overlays. That's just the SDK tagging DOM elements with attributes. **No token needed.** ✅

3. **The very first fetch** — before the live magic can start, the page has to grab *one* initial copy of the draft entry to render. **This is the only step that uses the backstage pass.**

So parts 1 and 2 — the actual "editors see their edits live" experience — never need the token. The token is only for that *single initial fetch* in part 3. And that fetch is exactly the thing you can move behind the counter:

> Instead of the browser walking up to Contentful's draft door with the pass, the browser asks **our own server** ("send a runner to grab the first draft"), and the runner (an MRT proxy endpoint) holds the pass. The pass never leaves the building. The browser still renders it, and live updates still stream in over postMessage.

That's *why* the doc (`02-contentful.md` §3) says "proxied through an MRT preview endpoint" — it's not asking you to give up client-side live preview; it's saying keep the pass on the server for that one fetch. You can ship **100% of the editor experience** with the token server-side.

**So "hand the token to the browser" is not the feature — it's one implementation shortcut for one step.** That reframes it into a real fork, and honestly both branches are legitimate:

- **Option A — keep the token server-side (what the doc says).** Point the Contentful client's `host` at an MRT proxy for the draft fetch; everything else (postMessage live updates, inspector) stays in the browser untouched. More plumbing, no doc change, no leak.
- **Option B — consciously accept the token in preview-only browsers.** This is a common, Contentful-blessed pattern for many teams, and it's simpler. But your doc *currently forbids it in writing* and classifies the CPA token as "semi-sensitive — exposes drafts" (§4). So choosing B means a deliberate policy change: update §3/§4/§9, get the Integration Lead to sign off, **and** hard-gate the token to non-prod in code so it can never leak on production.

Why it's not a shrug for Zimmermann specifically: that token in a browser bundle lets *anyone* who loads a preview-enabled env read **every unpublished draft** in the space — embargoed campaigns, unreleased collections, launch dates. For a luxury label, that's a real confidentiality surface, which is presumably why whoever wrote the doc already said "server-side only."

So it's not "the PR is wrong" so much as "the PR silently picked Option B, and Option B is a written-policy decision that's yours (with the Integration Lead) to make on purpose — not something to merge by default."

Which do you want? I'll spec the proxy for **A**, or draft the doc change + the non-prod gate for **B**.

message.content: what's the difference between the current coded implementation and how it should be?

content.text:
The difference is small and surgical — it's about **who holds the token and who the browser talks to**, not about how live preview works. Here's the concrete before/after.

## The essence
- **Now:** the browser holds the preview token and calls Contentful's draft API directly.
- **Should be:** the server holds the preview token; the browser calls *our* server, which calls Contentful.

Everything else — the live-update magic, inspector overlays, the `/preview` route, entry-type detection, locale logic — is **identical** in both. Only the fetch plumbing for that one initial draft read changes.

---

## Current implementation

**In the page (`contentfulPreview/index.tsx` + `experience/index.tsx`) — runs in the browser:**
```ts
const {spaceId, environment, previewAccessToken, accessToken} = getContentfulConfig()
const client = createClient({
  space: spaceId,
  environment,
  accessToken: previewAccessToken || accessToken,        // ⚠️ CPA token baked into client JS
  host: previewAccessToken ? 'preview.contentful.com'    // ⚠️ browser → Contentful directly
                           : 'cdn.contentful.com',
})
useFetchById({client, id: entryId, ...})                 // fetch executes in the browser
```

**And in `config/default.js:186–190`** the token is put where the bundle can see it:
```js
contentful: {
  accessToken:        process.env.CONTENTFUL_DELIVERY_TOKEN, // public — fine client-side
  previewAccessToken: process.env.CONTENTFUL_PREVIEW_TOKEN,  // ⚠️ serialized into the client bundle too
}
```
Flow: **`browser ──(CPA token)──▶ preview.contentful.com`**

---

## How it should be (Option A)

**1. Take the preview token out of the client config** — leave the public delivery token, drop the preview one from the serialized `app` config:
```js
// config/default.js
contentful: {
  spaceId:     process.env.CONTENTFUL_SPACE_ID,
  accessToken: process.env.CONTENTFUL_DELIVERY_TOKEN,   // stays — public, client-safe
  environment: process.env.CONTENTFUL_ENVIRONMENT_ID,
  // previewAccessToken removed from here — read server-side only
}
```

**2. Add a thin server-side proxy** that holds the token (lives in the SSR/request layer on MRT):
```ts
// server-only — has process.env, browser never sees the token
handle('/api/cms-preview/*', async (req, res) => {
  const token = process.env.CONTENTFUL_PREVIEW_TOKEN
  if (!token) return res.sendStatus(404)                       // no token → route off (e.g. prod)
  const upstream = await fetch(`https://preview.contentful.com/${req.params[0]}${query}`,
                               {headers: {Authorization: `Bearer ${token}`}})
  res.set('Cache-Control', 'no-store')                         // never cache drafts
  res.status(upstream.status).send(await upstream.text())
})
```

**3. Point the browser client at the proxy instead of Contentful** — same `createClient`, two fields change:
```ts
const client = createClient({
  space: spaceId,
  environment,
  accessToken: 'preview',          // dummy — the proxy swaps in the real token
  host: window.location.host,      // our storefront…
  basePath: '/api/cms-preview',    // …→ hits the proxy, not preview.contentful.com
})
```
Flow: **`browser ──▶ our MRT proxy ──(CPA token)──▶ preview.contentful.com`**

---

## What you *don't* touch (bounds the change)
- `ContentfulLivePreviewProvider`, `enableInspectorMode`, `enableLiveUpdates`, `targetOrigin` — unchanged.
- postMessage live updates + inspector overlays — unchanged (never used the token anyway).
- The published `/:slug` path — keeps the delivery token; as a **bonus, the bug is fixed** where it currently uses the preview token for all visitors when `CONTENTFUL_PREVIEW_TOKEN` is set (the token simply isn't in the client anymore, so it *can't*).

## The one catch for your A-vs-B call
That proxy has to live in the **SSR / `request-processor` layer, which is Tier 1** (Integration-Lead owned per `frozenFiles.md`). So Option A is contained code-wise (~1 small endpoint + 3 line changes), but it *does* reach into Integration-Lead territory — which is exactly the tradeoff against Option B (keep the client-side code, but change the doc + sign off + hard-gate to non-prod). That Tier-1 touch is probably the deciding factor.

Want me to draft either path?

message.content: provide me a simple to understand example of what blocker #1's use-case is and what the problem with it is?

content.text:
Here's a concrete story. Say Zimmermann's **staging** site has the preview token turned on so editors can preview drafts.

## The use-case (what it's *supposed* to do) ✅

1. **Priya**, a content editor, is building the **"Resort 2027"** campaign page in Contentful Studio. It's embargoed — launches in 3 weeks, hush-hush.
2. She clicks **"Open preview."** Studio opens the storefront inside an iframe at `https://staging.zimmermann.com/preview?entry=abc123`.
3. The page fetches her draft and renders it with real Zimmermann fonts, layout, and products. She tweaks the headline — it updates live.
4. Looks great. She's done. **This is exactly the feature working as intended.**

## The problem (what rode along in the browser) ⚠️

To do step 3, the browser needed the **preview token** to fetch the draft. In this PR, that token was shipped *inside the page's JavaScript* down to Priya's browser.

So if anyone opens that same page and hits **F12 → Network tab**, they see the request go out with the token sitting right there in plain text:

```
GET https://preview.contentful.com/spaces/zimm/entries/abc123?access_token=CFPA-9f3a...  ← the key, visible
```

And here's the kicker: **that token isn't a key to Priya's one page — it's the master key to the entire draft library.** With it copied, someone runs:

```
curl "https://preview.contentful.com/spaces/zimm/entries?access_token=CFPA-9f3a..."
```

…and pulls back **every unpublished draft in the space** — all unreleased collections, campaign copy, launch dates, pricing, imagery — weeks before any of it is public.

Who might grab it? Staging URLs leak all the time (pasted in Jira tickets, Slack, emails; sometimes crawled). An agency partner, a QA vendor, a contractor — anyone who can load that page can walk off with the master key. For a luxury label, a leaked Resort collection is a genuine commercial problem, not a theoretical one.

## The one-line contrast

- **This PR:** browser gets the master key → one DevTools copy = your whole draft library is exposed.
- **Correct version:** the key stays on Zimmermann's server; the browser just asks the server "render draft abc123." A snooper in DevTools sees a request to `staging.zimmermann.com/api/cms-preview/...` — **nothing to steal.**

That's the whole of blocker #1: not "previewing drafts is bad," but "the *key* that unlocks all drafts is being handed to every browser that loads the preview page."

message.content: how big of a refactor is needed to fix this concern?

content.text:
Honestly? **The code is small — it's not a rewrite.** The feature's React components, live-preview provider, inspector, routing, and entry-detection all stay exactly as they are. You're relocating *one HTTP call* from the browser to the server and adding a thin passthrough. Call it a **half-day to a day** of actual coding for someone who knows the SSR setup.

The catch isn't the size of the diff — it's *which files* the diff lands in.

## The work, sized

| Piece | Code size | Lands in |
|---|---|---|
| Drop `previewAccessToken` from client config | ~1 line (a deletion) | `config/default.js` — **absolute-frozen** 🔴 |
| New proxy endpoint (holds token, forwards to Contentful, `no-store`, 404 if no token) | ~30–40 lines | SSR server (`ssr.js`) — **absolute-frozen** 🔴 |
| Point the client's `host`/`basePath` at the proxy, drop the token | ~3 lines | The two page files (or one shared hook) — feature-owned ✅ |

## Why the real cost is coordination, not code
The two core changes both land in the **most locked-down files in the repo**. Per Hard Rule #4, `config/default.js` and `overrides/app/ssr.js` are *absolute* frozen — even a verified tier-1-approver session isn't allowed to auto-edit them. So this **can't ship as a solo feature PR**: the Integration Lead has to add the server route and the config change. That turns "a day of code" into "a day of code + a conversation with #integration and their review cycle."

That's genuinely the whole difficulty. The passthrough logic itself is boring — read env token, add an `Authorization` header, forward the request, don't cache. Low risk. The only technical gotchas are (a) make sure draft responses are never cached (`Cache-Control: no-store`), and (b) confirm the preview page still SSR-renders cleanly — both cheap.

## What does *not* change
The `/preview` route, the `ContentfulLivePreviewProvider`, inspector overlays, live updates via postMessage, locale logic, entry-type detection — untouched. Editors see zero difference. This is why it's a refactor of plumbing, not the feature.

## One honest caveat
End-to-end verification needs a **real Contentful preview environment** to test against — and per the integration doc's own open items (§10.3), those per-environment CPA credentials may not be provisioned yet. So the *coding* is a day; being able to *prove it works* could be gated on Contentful handing over a preview environment.

---

For contrast on your A-vs-B call: **Option B is even less code** — you'd keep the current client-side fetch and just add a hard "refuse if this is production" gate plus `noindex`, ~10 lines, all in feature-owned files. But B's "cost" isn't code either — it's getting the Integration Lead to sign off on *deliberately* shipping the preview token to browsers and updating the doc to match. So both roads run through #integration; A pays in plumbing, B pays in a written risk-acceptance.

Want me to spec the Option A proxy in enough detail to hand to the Integration Lead, or draft the Option B gate + doc change?

message.content: provide me a simple to understand example of what blocker #2's use-case is and what the problem with it is?

content.text:
Same world, same style. Quick honesty note up front so this stays distinct from #1: on a *correctly*-configured production (no preview token), `/preview` shows **published** content, not drafts. So this blocker isn't "drafts leak" — it's "**this editor-only door is standing wide open on the public customer site, and Google can walk through it.**"

## The use-case (what it's *supposed* to be) ✅

The `/preview` route exists as an **editor tool**. You paste `https://<host>/preview?entry=...` into Contentful's preview settings, and it loads inside Studio's iframe so editors can see their work. Its entire intended audience is editors, on the staging/preview environment. It should have **no reason to exist on `www.zimmermann.com`** at all.

## The problem (the door is open on the real site) ⚠️

The route is registered with no "not on production" gate and no `noindex`, so it's live and crawlable on the customer site. Two things go wrong:

**Everyday harm — SEO duplicate content:**
- Your Resort 2027 campaign has a clean, SEO-tuned URL: `www.zimmermann.com/resort-2027` — that's the one you want ranking.
- But the *identical* content is also reachable at `www.zimmermann.com/preview?entry=abc123` — ugly, parameterised, no canonical tag.
- Googlebot finds it (sitemap slip, a pasted link, plain crawling), and now indexes **two URLs for the same page**. Ranking signal splits, and Google may even surface the `/preview?entry=abc123` version in search results instead of your marketing URL. On a brand where search matters (it's called out all over AGENTS.md), that's a self-inflicted wound.
- There's also a "sneak peek" angle: a campaign that's *published* in Contentful but not yet linked anywhere (reveal scheduled for next week) can be pulled up early by anyone who hits `/preview?entry=<id>` — the back door serves it even though nothing on the site links to it.

**Why it's a *blocker*, not just cleanup — it's the missing safety net for #1:**
- Picture an ops change where someone copies staging's env vars to prod and accidentally brings `CONTENTFUL_PREVIEW_TOKEN` along.
- Because `/preview` is live and ungated on prod, that **one typo instantly turns the public production site into blocker #1's draft-library firehose** — on the real customer domain.
- If the route simply *didn't exist* on production, that same mistake would be harmless. So #2 is the guardrail that keeps a #1-style slip from becoming a public catastrophe. That's why the two are related but separate: #1 is "don't hand out the key," #2 is "don't leave the door installed on the building at all."

## The one-line fix
Make `/preview` exist **only where it's meant to be used** (editor/preview environments — e.g. 404 it when there's no preview token) and add **`noindex`** so search engines never touch it. It should not be sitting on `www.zimmermann.com` in the first place.

message.content: how big of a refactor is needed to fix this concern?

content.text:
Much smaller than #1 — and most of it comes **free with whichever #1 fix you pick.** The `noindex` half is genuinely trivial; the "not on prod" half is a couple of lines, and it largely piggybacks on #1. Call it **a couple of hours** if scoped alongside #1.

## The work, sized

| Piece | Code size | Lands in |
|---|---|---|
| `noindex` on the preview page (+ the `?preview` branch) | ~3–5 lines (a `<Seo noIndex>` — the pattern already exists in `pages/home/index.tsx:217`) | feature-owned page files ✅ |
| `Disallow: /preview` in `static/robots.txt` | 1 line | `static/robots.txt` — not protected ✅ |
| Gate the route so it's inert on prod | ~2 lines (conditionally register in `routes.tsx`) | `overrides/app/routes.tsx` — **Tier 2** 🟡 (cross-squad review, which this PR already needs) |
| …the on/off signal that gate reads | see below | depends on #1 |

## Why it's cheap: it rides on #1
The only non-trivial question is "how does the route know it's on production?" — and you almost certainly don't pay for that separately:

- **If you take #1 Option A (server-side proxy):** on prod the proxy already 404s (no token), so preview *can't function* on prod anyway. #2 then reduces to just adding `noindex` (trivial). The route gate becomes optional polish.
- **If you take #1 Option B (gate preview to non-prod):** that non-prod gate **is** #2's fix — you get "route off on prod" for the same line of code, then add `noindex`. One stone, both birds.

The *only* way #2 costs real coordination on its own is if you gate it with a brand-new `previewEnabled` boolean in `config/default.js` (frozen 🔴) — but even then it's a one-line, non-secret value, far softer than #1's token plumbing.

## One gotcha to get right
The gate signal must be **visible to both server and client** (a config boolean is), *not* a server-only value. If the server thinks the route exists and the client doesn't (or vice-versa), you get a React hydration mismatch. So gate on the client-safe flag, never on the server-held token directly.

## What doesn't change
The preview UX, the SDK wiring, the page components — all untouched. This is purely "where does the route live and can Google see it," not a logic change.

---

**Bottom line for planning:** don't scope #2 as its own ticket. Fold it into the #1 fix — when #1 lands, #2 is ~an hour of `noindex` + robots.txt on top. The two are one piece of work.

message.content: what's the connection of blocker #2 to blocker  #1? if blocker #1 gets resolved? are they to be fixed together?

content.text:
Great question — this is exactly the right thing to pin down before scoping the work. The short answer: **they're two layers of the same risk, they overlap in the worst case, but neither fully fixes the other — and whether resolving #1 also resolves #2 depends on which #1 option you pick.**

## The connection: key vs. door
- **#1 is about the key** — the preview token (which unlocks *all* drafts) leaking into the browser.
- **#2 is about the door** — the `/preview` route being installed on the public production site.

The catastrophic case is **both at once**: a public prod door (#2) + a token present (#1) = anyone on the internet pulls your entire draft library from `www.zimmermann.com`. That's why they feel linked. But they're *independent failure modes*, and each has a harm the other doesn't cover:

| | #1's leak (token in browser) | #2's harm (public crawlable route) |
|---|---|---|
| **On production** | Only bites *if* the token is misconfigured onto prod | **Always** bites — SEO duplicate content + the missing safety net |
| **On staging/preview** | **Always** bites (that's where preview runs, so the token is present and leaking) | Usually harmless (staging is access-controlled / robots-blocked) |

Read across: **#1's real bite is on staging** (where preview actually runs); **#2's real bite is on prod** (SEO + the open door). They hurt in *different places* — which is precisely why fixing one can't fully cover the other.

## If #1 gets resolved, is #2 auto-fixed?
Depends on the option:

- **Option A (server-side proxy):** #1 is fully fixed (token never in any browser). #2 is only *partly* covered — on prod the proxy 404s, so no draft leak even if someone hits the route. **But the route still exists and is still crawlable** (it just renders an error), so #2's SEO/duplicate-URL and "unnecessary public door" problems **remain**. You still have to add `noindex` + gate the route. **Not automatic.**

- **Option B (gate preview to non-prod):** Here they genuinely collapse into one fix. The single "don't run preview on production" gate is *simultaneously* how you keep the token off prod browsers (#1's prod exposure) **and** how you make the `/preview` route inert on prod (#2). Same line of code does both — plus a trivial `noindex`. *(Caveat: under B, the token still reaches browsers on staging by design — that's the accepted, signed-off tradeoff, not something B eliminates.)*

## Should they be fixed together?
**Yes — strongly, either way.** Three reasons:

1. **Same touch-points.** Both live in `routes.tsx`, the preview page, and the config — one PR, one cross-squad + Integration review cycle. Splitting them doubles the coordination overhead on the *same frozen files*.
2. **Same conceptual unit.** They're both "preview safety." Reviewers and QA will reason about them as one thing.
3. **Fixing one alone is a false "done."** Fix #1 but not #2 → the crawlable public door and safety-net gap stay. Fix #2 but not #1 → the key still leaks on staging, exactly where preview runs. Either half alone leaves a real hole.

**Bottom line:** treat them as **one piece of work**. Pick A or B for #1; #2 is then either mostly-free (B) or a small `noindex` + route-gate tail (A) bolted onto the same PR. Don't ticket them separately.

content.text:
Fair call on #3 — it's unrelated scope, so the clean move is just to drop it from *this* PR and let it ride separately; nothing to block on. Now the cleanups.

First, the useful reframe: **most of these aren't a separate chore.** They fold into the #1/#2 work — you'll be in these exact files and lines anyway. So the real question isn't "do a cleanup pass, yes/no," it's "which of these would I actually hold the PR for." Here's my honest triage.

## Genuinely needed (but they ride along with #1/#2)

**DRY — extract the duplicated client setup into one shared hook.**
*What it's for:* the `createClient` + `LivePreviewProvider` config is copy-pasted in both page files.
*Really needed?* **Yes — but not for tidiness.** This is *where the #1 fix lands.* You do not want to make a **security** change (routing the fetch through a proxy) in two places and hope they stay in sync — that's exactly how one copy gets fixed and the other keeps leaking. So it's a prerequisite that makes the #1 fix single-source and safe. Reframe it as "step 1 of fixing #1," not a cleanup.

**Hooks-order fix in `experience/index.tsx`.**
*What it's for:* `useFetchBySlug` is called *after* an early `return` — a Rules-of-Hooks violation that can crash on re-render.
*Really needed?* **Yes, but let me be honest about severity:** it's currently **dormant** — `client` is derived from stable env config, so it never actually flips null→non-null mid-life, so it likely never crashes *today*. It matters because (a) it's a real correctness violation, (b) the #1 change touches how the client is built, which could wake it up, and (c) the fix is nearly free — your *new* preview file already demonstrates the correct pattern. Fix it because you're in the file, not because it's on fire.

**SSR sanity-check.**
*What it's for:* `/preview` is server-rendered; if the live-preview wrapper touches `window` during render, the route 500s server-side.
*Really needed?* **Yes as a check — possibly zero code.** This is a *verification*, not a guaranteed change. The existing `/:slug` route already SSRs `ExperienceRoot` fine; the only new risk is `ContentfulLivePreviewProvider`. Load it once with SSR — if it renders, done; if it throws, wrap it or set the route `ssr: false`. Skip this and you risk the feature being broken in the editor iframe, so it's worth the five-minute check.

## Do-it-because-it's-free

**Remove the `console.log`.**
*What it's for:* it prints the detected type + locale on every preview load.
*Really needed?* **Low stakes, but just remove it.** It logs no secrets/PII, so it's not dangerous — but it's a clear standards violation (CodeRabbit *will* flag it) and it's a 5-second deletion. No reason to keep it. If you gate preview to non-prod anyway, it only ever ran in preview envs — even lower stakes. Don't agonise, just delete.

## Optional / I'd let these slide

**"Why" comments on the `as any` casts.**
*What it's for:* the TS rules want a reason next to each assertion, not just an eslint-disable.
*Really needed?* **No — cosmetic.** The casts are forced by the Contentful SDK's loose types; they won't cause bugs. It's genuinely free *if* you're already editing those lines (you will be, for the DRY/#1 work), so add them then. Not worth a dedicated pass.

**A unit test for the locale/token logic.**
*What it's for:* pins the "which locale, which token/host" resolution.
*Really needed?* **Not for the current code — but valuable *after* the refactor.** As-is the logic is nearly self-evident. Once you've extracted the hook and changed the fetch path for #1, a tiny test asserting *"preview mode routes through the proxy, not `preview.contentful.com`"* becomes a real **regression guard on the security fix** — that's when it earns its place. Add it with #1, not before.

---

**Bottom line:** there's no meaningful "cleanup pass" here. Two of them (**DRY**, **hooks-order**) are just *how you correctly implement #1*; one (**SSR check**) is a five-minute verification; the `console.log` is a reflex delete; and the last two (**cast comments, test**) are freebies that come along with the #1 refactor or can wait. So if you fix #1 and #2 properly, ~all of these come with it — you're not signing up for a separate list.
